sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory.
#
# Usage: backup.sh <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>_<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

source=${1%/}
dest=$2

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$dest"

base=$(basename "$source")
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}_${stamp}.tar.gz"

# Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths inside
# the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
tar -czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")" "$base"

echo "Created $archive"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Basic test: build a temporary source tree, run bin/backup.sh, and
# verify the archive exists and contains the expected files.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

dest_dir="$tmpdir/backups"

mkdir -p "$source_dir/data"
echo "hello" > "$source_dir/data/file1.txt"
echo "world" > "$source_dir/file2.txt"

bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_dir"

shopt -s nullglob
archives=("$dest_dir"/*.tar.gz)
if [[ ${#archives[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then

fi

echo "Archive: $archive"

  exit 1
}
tar -tzf "$archive" | grep -q "source/file2.txt" || {
  echo "FAIL: archive is missing source/file2.txt" >&2
  exit 1
}

echo "PASS: backup archive created and contents verified"

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, keep only the N newest
# archives matching the name pattern (default 7) and delete the rest.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

keep_daily=7

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$dest"

base=$(basename "$source")
stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

# Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths inside
# the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
tar -czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")" "$base"

echo "Created $archive"

rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"
```

```bash
# Delete the oldest archives beyond the newest $3, considering only files
# named <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz in $1. Fixed-width timestamps mean
# lexicographic order equals chronological order.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest=$1 base=$2 keep=$3
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$f")

  local total=${#candidates[@]}
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0

  local sorted i=0
  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    if (( i >= keep )); then
      echo "Removing old archive: $f"
      rm -- "$f"
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"
}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N  number of newest archives to keep (default 7)
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only archives matching the
# name pattern for this source are considered; the N newest are kept
# (fixed-width timestamps => lexicographic order == chronological order)
# and the rest are deleted.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

# Delete the oldest archives beyond the newest $3 in $1, considering only
# files named <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i=0 sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$f")
    fi
  done

  total=${#candidates[@]}
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    if (( i >= keep )); then
      echo "Removing old archive: $f"
      rm -- "$f"
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$dest"

base=$(basename "$source")
stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

# Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths inside
# the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
tar -czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")" "$base"

echo "Created $archive"

rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"
```

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7) and `--help`
- Has a test suite covering all functionality

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N
- [x] `tests/run.sh` — 5 tests:
  1. Basic backup (name format regex + contents check via `tar -tzf` capture)
  2. Rotation with default 7 (10 fakes + 1 real = 11, expects 7 remain, days 01–04 deleted)
  3. Rotation with `--keep-daily 3` (expects 3 remain)
  4. `--keep-daily 0` rejected (exit 2)
  5. `--help` exits 0 and contains "Usage:" and "--keep-daily"
- [x] All 5 tests passing

### In Progress
- [ ] (None — user's last request completed)

### Blocked
- (None)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`) mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order without parsing dates.
- **Rotation scope**: Only files matching `^<base>-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$` are considered; unrelated files in dest are never touched.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative (`source/file.txt`).
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario** (`backups`, `backups-rotation`, `backups-keep3`): Avoids cross-contamination and makes expected counts deterministic.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (`source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz`): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07), ensuring deterministic ordering.
- **Contents check via variable capture** (`listing=$(tar -tzf ...)`) instead of `tar | grep -q`: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.

2. Potential future features: additional rotation strategies (e.g., keep per-day only), `--dry-run`, logging, or other options

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N  number of newest archives to keep (default 7)
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered; the N newest are kept (fixed-width timestamps =>
# lexicographic order == chronological order) and the rest are deleted.
# Nothing outside <destination-dir> is ever touched.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--verify] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--verify] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate
out older archives.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep; older matching
                   archives are deleted (default: 7)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Delete the oldest archives beyond the newest $3 in $1. Candidates are
# collected as basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob, and deletions are
# always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 can be removed, and
# only names matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz are ever deleted.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i=0 sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total="${#candidates[@]}"
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i >= keep )); then
      echo "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
      rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7
verify=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$dest"

base=$(basename "$source")
stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

# Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths inside
# the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
tar -czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")" "$base"

echo "Created $archive"

if (( verify )); then
  listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
  if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
    echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
fi

rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"

**`tests/run.sh`** — new test 7 with a `source-excl` tree containing `data.txt`, `notes.tmp`, and a `.cache/tmp.bin`:
- **Control run** (no `--exclude`): asserts `.cache` *is* present, proving the exclusion is what changes the outcome.

GNU tar's `--exclude` matching is unanchored by default, so `--exclude .cache` matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree — confirmed by the passing test.

#   7. --exclude (repeatable): a .cache dir in the source is left out

edits.newText:
echo "--- Test 8: --dry-run ---"
dest_dry="$tmpdir/backups-dry"
mkdir -p "$dest_dry"
make_fake_archives "$dest_dry" 1 10

dry_out="$tmpdir/dry-out.txt"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dry" > "$dry_out" 2>&1 || fail "--dry-run should succeed"

# every output line must start with DRY:
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [[ "$line" == "DRY:"* ]] || fail "dry-run line does not start with 'DRY:' -> $line"
done < "$dry_out"

grep -q "^DRY: would create: $dest_dry/source-[0-9]\{8\}-[0-9]\{6\}\.tar\.gz$" "$dry_out" \
  || fail "missing DRY create line for the new archive"

del_count=$(grep -c "^DRY: would delete: " "$dry_out" || true)
# 10 existing + 1 to-be-created = 11, keep 7 => 4 oldest would be deleted
[[ "$del_count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 DRY delete lines, got $del_count"

# nothing was touched: all 10 fakes remain, no new archive was created
count=$(count_archives "$dest_dry" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 10 ]] || fail "dry-run changed the archive count: $count"

# a missing destination directory is not created either
dest_dry_new="$tmpdir/backups-dry-new"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dry_new" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "--dry-run with missing dest should succeed"
[[ ! -e "$dest_dry_new" ]] || fail "dry-run created the destination directory"
echo "PASS: --dry-run"

echo "PASS: all tests passed"

## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), and `--help`
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time — a basename from a flat-dir glob cannot contain `/`, so it's impossible to escape the destination

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates as basenames, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N, all deletions re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"`
- [x] `--verify` flag — after writing, runs `tar -tzf "$archive"`; fails (exit 1) if listing is empty; bonus: also catches corrupt archives via `set -e` on command substitution; verified **before** rotation
- [x] `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable, also `--exclude=PATTERN`) — patterns passed to tar as `--exclude`; empty patterns rejected (exit 2); built into a `tar_args` array
- [x] `tests/run.sh` — 7 tests:
  1. Basic backup (name format regex + contents check via `tar -tzf` capture)
  2. Rotation with default 7 + **stray survival** (three strays: `notes.txt` inside dest, `source-not-an-archive.tar.gz` inside dest matching `*.tar.gz` glob but not the timestamp pattern, `source-20260115-000000.tar.gz` **outside** dest matching full pattern — all must survive)
  3. Rotation with `--keep-daily 3` (expects 3 remain)
  4. `--keep-daily 0` rejected (exit 2)
  5. `--help` exits 0 and contains "Usage:" and "--keep-daily"
  6. `--verify`: happy path (output contains "Verified") + failure path (stub `tar` on PATH makes `-tzf` print nothing → script must exit non-zero)
  7. `--exclude` (repeatable): control run (no exclude) asserts `.cache` present; excluded run with `--exclude .cache --exclude notes.tmp` asserts both absent, `source-excl/data.txt` still present
- [x] All 7 tests passing
- [x] Committed as `3baa282111ee0f1b3a91105bda03bcfc3cf62a49` (root commit on `master`) with message "Add backup.sh with rotation and --verify, plus test suite" (repo-local identity: `sh-backup <sh-backup@localhost>`)

### In Progress
- [ ] (None — user's last request completed; `--exclude` is done and tested but not yet committed)

### Blocked
- (None)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`) mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order without parsing dates.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are collected as *basenames* from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz`, filtered by regex `^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$`, and every `rm` is `"${dest%/}/$b"`. A basename from a flat-dir glob cannot contain `/`, so deletion is structurally confined to the destination. This is stronger than a prefix-check guard because it's impossible to construct a path that escapes.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative (`source/file.txt`).
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: If `tar -tzf` itself errors (corrupt archive), the assignment propagates the failure — so verify catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup of older archives.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended in a loop, then `tar "${tar_args[@]}"`. Clean and extensible.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: `--exclude .cache` matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree (confirmed by passing test).
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario** (`backups`, `backups-rotation`, `backups-keep3`, `backups-verify`, `backups-excl`, `backups-excl-all`): Avoids cross-contamination and makes expected counts deterministic.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (`source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz`): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07), ensuring deterministic ordering.
- **Contents check via variable capture** (`listing=$(tar -tzf ...)`) instead of `tar | grep -q`: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: A fake `tar` script in `$tmpdir/fakebin` intercepts `-tzf` (exits 0, prints nothing) and passes `-czf` through to the real tar (captured via `command -v tar` before PATH change).
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: (1) not a `.tar.gz` at all, (2) a `.tar.gz` but not matching the timestamp pattern (exercises regex filter), (3) outside dest entirely but matching the full pattern (catches any bug that deletes by name alone or wanders outside the dest dir).

## Next Steps
1. User may ask to commit the `--exclude` feature (and possibly the rotation hardening + `--verify` if not already in the initial commit)
2. Potential future features: `--dry-run`, logging, compression level option, or other options

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]...
#                   [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        number of newest archives to keep (default 7)
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (every such line
#   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered; the N newest are kept (fixed-width timestamps =>
# lexicographic order == chronological order) and the rest are deleted.
# Nothing outside <destination-dir> is ever touched.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate
out older archives.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep; older matching
                   archives are deleted (default: 7)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (each line
                   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Delete the oldest archives beyond the newest $3 in $1. Candidates are
# collected as basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob, and deletions are
# always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 can be removed, and
# only names matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz are ever deleted.
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives that a real
# run would add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the keep
# threshold so the dry report matches what a real run would delete.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i=0 sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming >= keep )); then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        echo "DRY: would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        echo "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7
verify=0
excludes=()
dry_run=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    --exclude)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("$2")
      shift 2
      ;;
    --exclude=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--exclude=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("${1#--exclude=}")
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run)
      dry_run=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"
fi

base=$(basename "$source")
stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

if (( dry_run )); then
  # Report what would happen without touching anything (no mkdir, no
  # tar, no rm); incoming=1 accounts for the archive a real run would
  # create first, so the delete report matches a real run.
  echo "DRY: would create: $archive"
  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 1
else
  # Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths
  # inside the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
  tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")
  if (( ${#excludes[@]} > 0 )); then
    for pattern in "${excludes[@]}"; do
      tar_args+=(--exclude "$pattern")
    done
  fi
  tar_args+=("$base")
  tar "${tar_args[@]}"

  echo "Created $archive"

  if (( verify )); then
    listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
    if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
      echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
  fi

  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"
fi

```bash
# Acquire the destination lock (prevents two runs from rotating at once).
# Prefers flock(1) when available; falls back to a noclobber pidfile.
lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
lock_acquired=0

  if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! use_flock )); then
    rm -f -- "$lockfile"
  fi
}
trap cleanup_lock EXIT

if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  use_flock=1
  exec 9>"$lockfile"
  if ! flock -n 9; then
    echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2

  fi

  if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
    lock_acquired=1
  else
    # A lock file exists: check whether its owner is still running.
    holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile' (pid $holder); try again later" >&2

    fi

    echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2

      echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    lock_acquired=1
  fi
fi
```

```bash
if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
```

```bash
base=$(basename "$source")

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"

  # Hold an exclusive lock for the rest of the run so two runs cannot
  # rotate at the same time. Prefer flock(1) when available; otherwise
  # fall back to a noclobber pidfile (stale locks are detected via the
  # recorded pid and taken over). The lock file lives in the destination
  # and is not a *.tar.gz, so rotation never touches it.
  lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
  lock_acquired=0
  lock_use_flock=0
  cleanup_lock() {
    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else
      holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
      if ! ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi
  fi
fi

archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"
```

+mkdir -p "$slowbin"
+cat > "$slowbin/tar" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+if [[ "\$1" == "-czf" ]]; then
+  sleep 2
+fi
+exec "$real_tar" "\$@"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$slowbin/tar"
+
+lockfile="$dest_lock/backup-source.lock"
+PATH="$slowbin:$PATH" bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$tmpdir/lock-run1.out" 2>&1 &
+run1=$!
+
+# Wait until run 1 actually holds the lock (up to ~15s)
+held=0
+if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  exec 8>"$lockfile"
+  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
+    if ! flock -n 8; then
+      held=1
+      break
+    fi
+    sleep 0.1
+  done
+  exec 8>&-
+else
+  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
+    if [[ -e "$lockfile" ]]; then
+      held=1
+      break
+    fi
+    sleep 0.1
+  done
+fi
+(( held )) || fail "timed out waiting for run 1 to hold the lock"
+
+# The second run must exit 3 with a clear message, without touching dest
+lock_out2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.out"
+lock_err2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.err"
+set +e
+bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out2" 2> "$lock_err2"
+rc=$?
+set -e
+[[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]] || fail "second concurrent run should exit 3, got $rc"
+grep -qi "lock" "$lock_err2" || fail "stderr of the locked-out run does not mention the lock: $(cat "$lock_err2")"
+[[ -z "$(cat "$lock_out2")" ]] || fail "locked-out run printed to stdout"
+
+# Run 1 must still complete normally once it finishes
+wait "$run1" || fail "first (lock-holding) run should have succeeded"
+count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
+[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after run 1 (3 fakes + new), got $count"
+echo "PASS: lock file prevents concurrent runs (exit 3)"
+
 echo "PASS: all tests passed"

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, and `--help`
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, unknown options)
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time — a basename from a flat-dir glob cannot contain `/`, so it's impossible to escape the destination
- All dry-run output lines must start with `DRY:` (enforced in test)
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, unknown options)

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates as basenames, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N, all deletions re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"`
- [x] `--verify` flag — after writing, runs `tar -tzf "$archive"`; fails (exit 1) if listing is empty; verified **before** rotation
- [x] `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable, also `--exclude=PATTERN`) — patterns passed to tar as `--exclude`; empty patterns rejected (exit 2); built into a `tar_args` array
- [x] `--dry-run` flag — prints `DRY: would create: <archive>` and `DRY: would delete: <path>` lines; skips mkdir, tar, verify, rm; uses `incoming=1` parameter so delete report matches what a real run would do
- [x] Missing source directory exits with code **2** (changed from 1), error to stderr
- [x] `tests/run.sh` — 9 tests:
  1. Basic backup (name format regex + contents check via `tar -tzf` capture)
  2. Rotation with default 7 + **stray survival** (three strays: `notes.txt` inside dest, `source-not-an-archive.tar.gz` inside dest matching `*.tar.gz` glob but not the timestamp pattern, `source-20260115-000000.tar.gz` **outside** dest matching full pattern — all must survive)
  3. Rotation with `--keep-daily 3` (expects 3 remain)
  4. `--keep-daily 0` rejected (exit 2)
  5. `--help` exits 0 and contains "Usage:" and "--keep-daily"
  6. `--verify`: happy path (output contains "Verified") + failure path (stub `tar` on PATH makes `-tzf` print nothing → script must exit non-zero)
  7. `--exclude` (repeatable): control run (no exclude) asserts `.cache` present; excluded run with `--exclude .cache --exclude notes.tmp` asserts both absent, `source-excl/data.txt` still present
  8. `--dry-run`: every line starts with `DRY:`, correct `DRY: would create:` pattern, exactly 4 `DRY: would delete:` lines (10 existing + 1 incoming = 11, keep 7 → 4 deleted), archive count unchanged at 10, missing dest dir not created
  9. Missing source directory: exit code 2, stderr contains "source directory", stdout is empty
- [x] All 9 tests passing
- [x] ShellCheck clean on both `bin/backup.sh` and `tests/run.sh`
- [x] Commit `3baa282` — "Add backup.sh with rotation and --verify, plus test suite"
- [x] Commit `d7e8a93` — "Add --dry-run: report create/delete as DRY: lines, touch nothing"

### In Progress
- [ ] (None — awaiting user direction; exit-code change is uncommitted)

### Blocked
- (None)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`) mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order without parsing dates.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are collected as *basenames* from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz`, filtered by regex `^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$`, and every `rm` is `"${dest%/}/$b"`. A basename from a flat-dir glob cannot contain `/`, so deletion is structurally confined to the destination.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative (`source/file.txt`).
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: If `tar -tzf` itself errors (corrupt archive), the assignment propagates the failure — so verify catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup of older archives.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended in a loop, then `tar "${tar_args[@]}"`.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: `--exclude .cache` matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree (confirmed by passing test).
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination and makes expected counts deterministic.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (`source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz`): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07), ensuring deterministic ordering.
- **Contents check via variable capture** (`listing=$(tar -tzf ...)`) instead of `tar | grep -q`: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: A fake `tar` script in `$tmpdir/fakebin` intercepts `-tzf` (exits 0, prints nothing) and passes `-czf` through to the real tar.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: (1) not a `.tar.gz` at all, (2) a `.tar.gz` but not matching the timestamp pattern, (3) outside dest entirely but matching the full pattern.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter for accurate delete count**: In a real run the new archive occupies the newest slot (index 0 in the sorted list), shifting all existing archives down by one. The `incoming` parameter (default 0 for real runs where the archive is already on disk; 1 for dry-run where it isn't yet) shifts the keep threshold: `i + incoming >= keep`. This makes the dry-run report exactly match what a real run would delete, including edge cases like `--keep-daily 1`.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" means the destination directory is not created either (verified in test).
- **Exit code 2 for missing source** (was 1): Consistent with all other argument/validation errors (`--keep-daily 0`, unknown options). The check happens before `mkdir -p "$dest"`, so a missing source also leaves the destination untouched.

## Next Steps
1. User may ask to commit the exit-code change (`exit 1` → `exit 2`) + test 9
2. Potential future features: logging, compression level option, `--source` validation improvements, or other options

## Critical Context
- Working directory: `/work/sh-backup/`
- File tree: `bin/backup.sh`, `tests/run.sh` (both executable)
- Current git state: two commits on `master`:
  - `3baa282` — "Add backup.sh with rotation and --verify, plus test suite"
  - `d7e8a93` — "Add --dry-run: report create/delete as DRY: lines, touch nothing"
- **Uncommitted changes**: `exit 1` → `exit 2` in source check in `backup.sh`; test 9 in `run.sh`
- Repo-local git identity: `sh-backup <sh-backup@localhost>`
- Test source trees: `$tmpdir/source` (data/file1.txt, file2.txt), `$tmpdir/source-excl` (data.txt, notes.tmp, .cache/tmp.bin)
- `rotate_old_archives()` signature: `rotate_old_archives() { local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}"; ... }` — uses `"${dest%/}/$b"` for deletion, `i + incoming >= keep` for threshold
- `dry_run` global variable (0/1), initialized alongside `keep_daily=7`, `verify=0`, `excludes=()`
- In dry-run branch: `echo "DRY: would create: $archive"` then `rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 1`
- In real-run branch: tar, echo "Created", optional verify, then `rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"` (incoming defaults to 0)
- Source check: `if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2; exit 2; fi`
- `mkdir -p "$dest"` is conditional: `if (( ! dry_run )); then mkdir -p "$dest"; fi`

Wait — same problem in reverse: the subshell opens fd 8 (its own new OFD — a fresh open(2) creates a new OFD), `flock -n 8` locks that new OFD; if it succeeds, the subshell exits → its OFD is closed → the lock is released. If it fails (someone else is holding it), no lock was acquired. So a per-iteration subshell is safe: each `open` creates a **new** OFD, and the lock only exists while that subshell's flock utility (child process) is alive... hmm, wait, actually no!

Let me redo this: in a subshell `( exec 8>file; flock -n 8 )`:
- The subshell opens the file → new OFD_A (separate from the holder's OFD_B).
- The `flock -n 8` utility is forked from the subshell, inheriting fd 8 → OFD_A.
- If free: the utility locks OFD_A (no contention since it's a different OFD), exits → its fd is closed, but the subshell's fd 8 (same OFD_A) is still open → the lock on OFD_A persists until the subshell exits. The subshell exits immediately after → the lock is released.
- If the holder is holding OFD_B: the utility's `flock -n` on OFD_A fails (cross-OFD contention on the same inode) → exit code 1 → the subshell exits 1 → OFD_A is closed, no lock was held to begin with.

So per-iteration subshell polling works! The lock acquired by the "free" case lives only for a moment inside the subshell.

But wait — isn't there a race: the subshell's OFD_A lock is acquired and then (immediately after) released by the subshell's exit. Between acquire and release, the holder... we don't care, we already got our answer "free". No problem.

**Option B** (cleaner): Don't use `flock(1)` for polling at all. Poll with a `flock ... -c true` form on the file? Same OFD problem? The `flock file -c cmd` form: opens the file itself (its own OFD), locks it, runs the command, and closes on exit → released. So:

```bash
if flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
  # free
else
  # held
fi
```
`flock -n "$lockfile" -c true`: the utility opens the file (its own OFD), tries LOCK_EX|NB, runs `true`, exits, and closes → released. If held by run1 → fails with exit code 1. This is much cleaner — no fd juggling in the test shell!

Wait, but be careful: does `flock file -c true` leave the lock held? The utility holds the fd itself (not inherited from the shell), exits after the command → fd closed → released. Yes, clean.

So the poller becomes:
```bash
for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
  if ! flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
    held=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done
```
No exec, no fd 8.

Hmm, wait — but actually, the same OFD inheritance subtlety affects the **script** itself too! In backup.sh: `exec 9>"$lockfile"` (the script's shell holds fd 9 → OFD_S) followed by `flock -n 9` → the utility inherits fd 9 → locks OFD_S. If acquisition succeeds, the utility exits, and the script's fd 9 keeps OFD_S open → **the lock is held by the script** — that's exactly the behavior we want (held until the script exits). If acquisition fails, the utility exits 1, and the script exits with exit code 3 — but wait, did the failed attempt leave a lock? No — a failed flock(-n) doesn't lock. But: could a **previous** script run have left a lock on OFD_S? OFD_S is unique to this script process; when the script exits, fd 9 closes → OFD_S dies → the lock is released. So for the script, the "lock persists as long as any fd is open" behavior is precisely the desired semantics.

And this also explains the classic idiom `exec 9>lockfile; flock -n 9` — the standard pattern, and it works as intended. The pitfall was only in my **polling** in the test: I was using the same shell fd for the check, and a **successful** non-blocking check was inadvertently acquiring a lock that persisted (because the shell kept the fd open).

Hmm wait, one more check on the script side: could the same "success acquires a persistent lock" problem bite us in the script's **second** execution? No — each script run opens its own fd 9 (new OFD). Cross-run contention: run2's `flock -n 9` on its own OFD_2 vs. run1's OFD_1 (locked) → fails → exit code 3. Correct.

So the only fix needed is the test's poller: use `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` (no shell fd).

Also, the fallback branch of the test (no flock) is fine (it just checks for file existence).

Let me double-check `flock -n file -c true` — man page: `flock [options] file|directory -c command`. `-c` runs the command via $SHELL. Exit status: 1 if it couldn't acquire (default without -E). Good.

Actually, hmm — does `flock file -c true` have a subtle problem of blocking... no, with -n it's non-blocking.

Also, `2>/dev/null` to suppress "unable to open" etc.

Let me update the test:

```bash
held=0
for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
  if ! flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
    held=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done
```

Wait, but this only applies if flock is available; otherwise, file existence check. Keep the if/else:

```bash
held=0
if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
    if ! flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
      held=1
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.1
  done
else
  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 150; attempt++ )); do
    if [[ -e "$lockfile" ]]; then
      held=1
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.1
  done
fi
```

Wait, one more consideration: `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` in the "free" case briefly acquires the lock on its own OFD and releases it on exit. Could that brief acquisition interfere with run1's `flock -n 9`? Timing: the poller's flock utility is alive for about 1ms (running `true`). If run1 tries to acquire exactly during that 1ms → run1 fails → exits 3 → then the poller... run1 exits 3 → the poller keeps polling (lock free) → timeout → test failure. This is a small race, but the window is tiny (about 1ms per iteration × 150 iterations). Hmm. run1 takes about 100-300ms to reach flock; the collision probability per iteration is about 1-2%... over 150 iterations it might actually bite occasionally. Hmm.

Can we eliminate the race entirely? Alternative: **hold the lock yourself from the test** as the "first run" — the original simpler design! That is:

- The test starts a `flock "$lockfile" -c 'sleep 5' &` holder (which uses its own OFD, holds for 5 seconds, and releases on exit).
- Poll with `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` until the holder actually holds it (the brief lock acquisition in the free case doesn't matter. Once the holder is holding, the poller's attempt fails → we detect the held state. The only race is the detection being one iteration late — no problem).
- Then run the script → exit code 3.
- Then let the holder finish (or kill it).
- Then run the script again → this time expect exit code 0 (bonus: proves the lock was released and normal operation works)!

This is deterministic: no dependence on run1's timing at all. But it's less end-to-end (the holder isn't an actual backup run).

Hybrid (best of both): keep the slow-tar run1 as the holder (real end-to-end), but poll with a non-holding check. The race (run1's single flock attempt colliding with the poller's 1ms window) — run1 does exactly **one** `flock -n 9` attempt (on failure it exits 3 — and that's exactly what happened before: run1 got "locked out" by the test's own lingering lock). To protect run1, instead of a single attempt, we can make run1 **retry**: e.g., the fake tar sleeps 2 seconds before tar — but the lock is acquired **before** tar (in the script). run1's flock attempt happens at script startup (~100ms), at which point the poller is actively polling. The race window is real, but let's quantify: the poller's `flock -n file -c true` holds the lock from open until exit ≈ fork+exec+lock+true+exit ≈ 1-5ms. Polling period = 100ms. Duty cycle ≈ 5%. run1 has one attempt at t≈50-300ms → collision probability per test run ≈ 5-15%?? That's too flaky.

Fix: make the poller check "is the lockfile locked" without ever holding the lock. Options:
1. `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` — briefly holds (the race above).
2. Check via /proc/locks! Parse /proc/locks for the inode of the lockfile → if a flock entry exists for that inode, it's held. No acquisition. Deterministic, no race. But /proc/locks parsing in bash is... possible: get the inode with `stat -c %i "$lockfile"`, then grep /proc/locks for "FL" and the inode. /proc/locks lines: `1: FLOCK  ADVISORY  WRITE pid:fd mode:inode ...` the format varies: e.g. `4: FLOCK  ADVISORY  WRITE 1234:5 102:123456 0 0 kernel 0`. The last "kernel" entry... parsing is fragile but doable: `grep -E "FLOCK.*:${inode} " /proc/locks`. Hmm, the inode field is `dev:inode`. So match `:[[:space:]]*$inode[[:space:]]`... this is fragile across kernel versions.

3. Have run1 retry the lock a few times (make the script itself robust against a brief lock): in backup.sh, retry `flock -n 9` a few times with small sleeps before giving up? This changes the script's semantics (waits briefly) — actually, is that desirable? "A second run should exit with exit code 3" — a short retry (e.g., 5×100ms) doesn't change the observable behavior in tests (the holder holds for 2 seconds), and it makes the script robust against lock handoff. But it adds complexity and changes the timing.

4. Reverse the test structure to eliminate the race: start run1 and have the poller wait for **evidence** that run1 is holding the lock in a way that involves no acquisition at all: the only acquisition-free check is /proc/locks or `fuser`... hmm.

5. **Poll the lockfile's mtime/ctime?** No — creation isn't the same as holding (run1 opens the fd before locking — almost simultaneously; after `exec 9>` (creation), lock acquisition is within microseconds. But the test might see the file and poll before run1's lock... if we poll with flock -n, it's free → keep waiting. Fine — the race only matters when run1's one-shot attempt collides with the poller's 1-5ms window).

6. Simplest and most robust: **poll for run1's lockfile + poll with `flock -n file -c true`, but start polling only after run1 has clearly passed the lock point.** How do we know run1 has passed it? run1 sleeps 2 seconds in tar — its first output "Created ..." appears after tar. Not before the lock.

7. Make the fake tar's sleep the slow part **and** have run1 retry the lock: actually — let me reconsider. How about the test's poller first waits for the lockfile to exist (run1 created it → means it reached `exec 9>`, i.e., is about to lock or is locked), and **then** does a single `flock -n file -c true` check. Timeline: the file exists only after run1's `exec 9>` — which is 2 instructions before `flock -n 9` (microseconds). So when the test sees the file, run1 locks within microseconds. The test then tries `flock -n -c true` — if free (run1 hasn't locked yet, microseconds), the test briefly acquires → the collision risk remains, but the window is now much smaller (microseconds instead of ~100ms). And crucially, the test only does that one check... no wait, the test polls in a loop until held.

Honestly, the cleanest and fully deterministic design is: **the test itself is the initial holder** (option above), plus run1 as verification that normal runs work:

- Step 1: holder = `flock "$lockfile" -c 'sleep 5' &` — holds for 5 seconds.
- Step 2: poll `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` until it fails (holder is holding). (Brief acquisition during free is fine — at most we wait one extra iteration; no other contender exists yet.)
- Step 3: run the script (real, fast tar — no fake tar needed!) → expect exit code 3, stderr contains "lock", stdout empty.
- Step 4: wait for the holder to finish (≤5 seconds) — or kill it; then verify the script now works: run the script → exit code 0, archive created. (This also proves the lock is released when the holder exits — good semantics check.)

This is fully deterministic — no slow tar, no collision (step 2 has no contender; step 3 has a single contender — the 5-second holder — no polling in parallel; step 4 runs after the holder is gone).

But does it test that "two real runs don't rotate simultaneously"? Indirectly: the script contends against a lock held on the same file in the same protocol. The script's own lock holding (step 4's normal run) is covered by all the other tests (rotation works). I think this is solid.

Hmm, but I also like the end-to-end version (a slow run1 holding the lock across tar+rotate). The race is only a problem because the script tries the lock once. Alternative: keep the slow run1 and have the test poll /proc/locks (no acquisition). Let me check /proc/locks format here.

Actually, you know what — let me first check /proc/locks; if it's parseable here, the end-to-end test stays fully deterministic.

content.text:
**Found it — a classic `flock(1)` pitfall.** The poller's `flock -n 8` was *succeeding* (lock free), which meant it was **acquiring** the lock on the shared open file description, and the test shell's fd 8 was keeping it held for the entire 15-second loop — so run 1 really was being locked out by the test itself.

Let me check `/proc/locks` for an acquisition-free way to check:

arguments.command:
tmp=$(mktemp -d); f="$tmp/l"; touch "$f"
inode=$(stat -c %i "$f")
echo "inode=$inode"
( exec 9>"$f"; flock 9; sleep 1 ) &
sleep 0.3
echo "=== /proc/locks ==="
cat /proc/locks
echo "=== grep by inode ==="
grep -c "FLOCK.* [0-9]*:${inode} " /proc/locks || echo "no match"
wait
rm -rf "$tmp"

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, and `--help`
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- All dry-run output lines must start with `DRY:` (enforced in test)
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, unknown options)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates as basenames, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N, all deletions re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"`
- [x] `--verify` flag — after writing, runs `tar -tzf "$archive"`; fails (exit 1) if listing is empty; verified **before** rotation
- [x] `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable, also `--exclude=PATTERN`) — patterns passed to tar as `--exclude`; empty patterns rejected (exit 2); built into a `tar_args` array
- [x] `--dry-run` flag — prints `DRY: would create:` and `DRY: would delete:` lines; skips mkdir, tar, verify, rm
- [x] Missing source directory exits with code **2**, error to stderr
- [x] `tests/run.sh` — 9 tests (basic backup, rotation default, rotation keep-3, keep-daily-0, help, verify, exclude, dry-run, missing source)
- [x] All 9 original tests passing
- [x] ShellCheck clean on both `bin/backup.sh` and `tests/run.sh`
- [x] Commit `3baa282` — "Add backup.sh with rotation and --verify, plus test suite"
- [x] Commit `d7e8a93` — "Add --dry-run: report create/delete as DRY: lines, touch nothing"
- [x] Lock file implementation in `bin/backup.sh`:
  - Lock file: `$dest/backup-${base}.lock` (not a `*.tar.gz`, so rotation ignores it)
  - **flock path**: `exec 9>"$lockfile"` → `flock -n 9` → exit 3 with message if held
  - **Fallback (no flock)**: noclobber pidfile (`set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile"`) with stale-lock detection via `kill -0`; trap-based cleanup on exit
  - Dry-run skips locking entirely
  - Header comment documents the concurrency model
- [x] Test 10 added to `tests/run.sh` (slow tar stub, background run 1, poll for lock, run 2 expects exit 3)

### In Progress
- [ ] Debugging test 10 timeout: the polling loop reports "timed out waiting for run 1 to hold the lock" even though manual testing confirms flock works correctly. The mechanism is proven to work in isolation (manual test shows `LOCK HELD` after 1s, run 1 exits 0). Need to determine why the in-test polling doesn't see the held lock.

### Blocked
- (None)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are basenames from a flat-dir glob; every `rm` re-anchors to `"${dest%/}/$b"`.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative.
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: Catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: Matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree.
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates**: Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07).
- **Contents check via variable capture**: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: Fake `tar` intercepts `-tzf`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: not-a-tar.gz, tar.gz-but-wrong-pattern, outside-dest.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter**: Shifts keep threshold so dry-run report matches real-run behavior.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" includes the destination directory.
- **Exit code 2 for missing source**: Consistent with all other argument/validation errors.
- **Lock file naming: `backup-<base>.lock`** (per-source, not per-dest): Allows different sources backing up to the same destination to run in parallel since each only deletes its own pattern. The name doesn't match `*.tar.gz` so rotation ignores it.
- **Lock acquired after `mkdir -p "$dest"` and before any mutation**: Ordering ensures the dest exists for the lock file, and the lock protects all subsequent operations (tar, verify, rotate).
- **flock preferred, noclobber pidfile fallback**: flock is automatically released on process exit (fd close), no stale locks. The noclobber fallback writes `$$` and checks liveness with `kill -0` for stale detection. Trap removes the fallback lock file on normal exit.
- **Dry-run takes no lock**: Acquiring a lock requires creating the lock file, which would violate "don't touch anything." Dry-run is read-only so no protection needed.
- **Test 10 uses a slow tar stub (sleep 2 on -czf)**: Makes run 1 hold the lock long enough for run 2 to start and observe contention. Polling (not fixed sleep) waits for the lock to actually be held before testing run 2.
- **Test polling: `flock -n 8` on an fd opened by the test shell**: Deterministic — waits until the holder actually holds the lock (not just until the file exists). For the fallback path, polls for file existence.
- **Test 10 asserts 4 archives after run 1 completes** (3 fakes + 1 new, keep 7 → all kept): Confirms run 1 actually created its archive.

## Next Steps
1. Debug why test 10's polling loop times out despite the mechanism working in isolation. Likely causes to investigate:
   - Whether `flock -n 8` behaves differently when fd 8 was opened by `exec 8>` in the test shell vs. a standalone command
   - Whether the `sleep 0.1` in the polling loop is actually sleeping (fractional sleep support)
   - Whether run 1 is failing before it reaches the lock acquisition in the test context (inspect `lock-run1.out`)
   - Whether the `for (( ... ))` loop or `(( attempt = 0; ... ))` syntax is behaving unexpectedly under `set -euo pipefail`
2. Once fixed, run full test suite + ShellCheck
3. Commit all uncommitted changes (exit-code change + test 9 + lock file + test 10)

## Critical Context
- Working directory: `/work/sh-backup/`
- File tree: `bin/backup.sh`, `tests/run.sh` (both executable)
- Current git state: two commits on `master`:
  - `3baa282` — "Add backup.sh with rotation and --verify, plus test suite"
  - `d7e8a93` — "Add --dry-run: report create/delete as DRY: lines, touch nothing"
- **Uncommitted changes**: exit-code change (exit 1→2 for missing source), test 9, lock file implementation in `backup.sh`, test 10 in `run.sh`
- Repo-local git identity: `sh-backup <sh-backup@localhost>`
- Test source trees: `$tmpdir/source` (data/file1.txt, file2.txt), `$tmpdir/source-excl` (data.txt, notes.tmp, .cache/tmp.bin)
- `rotate_old_archives()` signature: `rotate_old_archives() { local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}"; ... }`
- `dry_run` global variable (0/1), `keep_daily=7`, `verify=0`, `excludes=()`
- Lock block in `backup.sh` (inside `if (( ! dry_run ))`):
  ```bash
  lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
  lock_acquired=0
  lock_use_flock=0
  cleanup_lock() {
    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else
      holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
      if ! ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi
  fi
  ```
- Test 10 structure in `tests/run.sh`:
  - Creates `$dest_lock` with 3 fake archives
  - Creates a slow tar stub in `$slowbin` (sleeps 2s on `-czf`, then execs real tar)
  - Starts run 1 in background with `PATH="$slowbin:$PATH"`
  - Polls for lock: if flock available, opens fd 8 on lockfile and loops `flock -n 8` (up to 150×0.1s); else polls for file existence
  - Runs run 2 (normal PATH), captures rc/stdout/stderr
  - Asserts rc=3, stderr contains "lock" (case-insensitive), stdout empty
  - `wait "$run1"`, asserts 4 archives exist
- Manual debug confirmed: flock is at `/usr/bin/flock`, mechanism works (lock file created, `flock -n 8` reports HELD, run 1 exits 0)
- The test file has been read back at offset 230 confirming the edit was applied correctly
- `awk` is NOT available in this environment (test extraction failed)
- `real_tar` variable is defined in test 6 and is in scope for test 10

- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.

- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

**The test-10 timeout mystery** — the polling loop was the bug, not the lock. `flock(2)` locks are attached to the *open file description*: when the test's `flock -n 8` probe succeeded (lock free), it *acquired* the lock, and the test shell's fd 8 kept that OFD alive for the whole 15 s loop. - the test itself holds the lock: `flock "$lockfile" -c 'sleep 5' &` (flock path) or a live-pid pidfile (fallback path)
- polls with `flock -n "$lockfile" -c true` until the holder actually holds it

- after `wait $holder`, asserts a normal run succeeds and creates its archive

content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]...
#                   [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        number of newest archives to keep (default 7)
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (every such line
#   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered; the N newest are kept (fixed-width timestamps =>
# lexicographic order == chronological order) and the rest are deleted.
# Nothing outside <destination-dir> is ever touched.
#
# Concurrency: each run holds an exclusive lock on
# <destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock for the whole
# create+rotate (flock(1) when available, else a noclobber pidfile);
# a second concurrent run exits 3. --dry-run takes no lock.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate
out older archives.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep; older matching
                   archives are deleted (default: 7)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (each line
                   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Delete the oldest archives beyond the newest $3 in $1. Candidates are
# collected as basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob, and deletions are
# always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 can be removed, and
# only names matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz are ever deleted.
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives that a real
# run would add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the keep
# threshold so the dry report matches what a real run would delete.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i=0 sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming >= keep )); then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        echo "DRY: would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        echo "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7
verify=0
excludes=()
dry_run=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    --exclude)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("$2")
      shift 2
      ;;
    --exclude=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--exclude=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("${1#--exclude=}")
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run)
      dry_run=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi

base=$(basename "$source")

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"

  # Hold an exclusive lock for the rest of the run so two runs cannot
  # rotate at the same time. Prefer flock(1) when available; otherwise
  # fall back to a noclobber pidfile (a stale lock is detected via the
  # recorded pid and taken over). The lock file lives in the
  # destination and is not a *.tar.gz, so rotation never touches it.
  lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
  lock_acquired=0
  lock_use_flock=0
  cleanup_lock() {
    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else
      holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
      if ! ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi
  fi
fi

stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

if (( dry_run )); then
  # Report what would happen without touching anything (no mkdir, no
  # tar, no rm); incoming=1 accounts for the archive a real run would
  # create first, so the delete report matches a real run.
  echo "DRY: would create: $archive"
  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 1
else
  # Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths
  # inside the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
  tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")
  if (( ${#excludes[@]} > 0 )); then
    for pattern in "${excludes[@]}"; do
      tar_args+=(--exclude "$pattern")
    done
  fi
  tar_args+=("$base")
  tar "${tar_args[@]}"

  echo "Created $archive"

  if (( verify )); then
    listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
    if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
      echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
  fi

  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily"
fi
