#      must survive
#   3. rotation honoring --keep-daily 3
#   4. --keep-daily validation
#   5. --help output
#   6. --verify: succeeds on a good archive, fails on an empty listing
#   7. --exclude (repeatable): a .cache dir in the source is left out
#   8. --dry-run: reports create/delete with DRY: lines, touches nothing
#   9. missing source directory: error to stderr, exit 2, nothing printed
#      to stdout
#   10. lock file: a concurrent second run exits 3; the first run still
#        completes and creates its archive
#   11. --keep-weekly retention: the keep set is the union of the daily keep
#        set and the newest archive of each of the last N ISO weeks
#   12. --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention
#   13. --keep-weekly validation (negative / non-numeric rejected, 0 ok)
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

source_dir="$tmpdir/source"
dest_dir="$tmpdir/backups"

mkdir -p "$source_dir/data"
echo "hello" > "$source_dir/data/file1.txt"
echo "world" > "$source_dir/file2.txt"

fail() {
  echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Count archives in $1 that match <source basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.
count_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2"
  local n=0 f b
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      n=$(( n + 1 ))
    fi
  done
  printf '%s' "$n"
}

# Create fake "old" archives in $1 named source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz
# for January days $2..$3 (fixed past dates, one file per day).
make_fake_archives() {
  local dest="$1" first="$2" last="$3"
  local i f
  for (( i = first; i <= last; i++ )); do
    f="$dest/source-202601$(printf '%02d' "$i")-000000.tar.gz"
    touch "$f"
  done
}

# Compute YYYYMMDD for a date relative to the current ISO week: $1 = number of
# weeks before this week (0 = this week), $2 = day offset into that week
# (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday). Anchoring to the real current week keeps the
# weekly fixtures correct no matter which day of the week the suite runs on.
week_date() {
  local weeks_back="$1" day_offset="$2"
  local dow monday_epoch target
  dow=$(date -u +%u)
  monday_epoch=$(date -u -d "today - $((dow - 1)) days" +%s)
  target=$(( monday_epoch - weeks_back * 7 * 86400 + day_offset * 86400 ))
  date -u -d "@$target" +%Y%m%d
}

echo "--- Test 1: basic backup ---"
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_dir"

shopt -s nullglob
archives=("$dest_dir"/*.tar.gz)
[[ ${#archives[@]} -gt 0 ]] || fail "no archive found in $dest_dir"
archive="${archives[0]}"
echo "Archive: $archive"

name=$(basename "$archive")
re="^$(basename "$source_dir")-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$"
[[ "$name" =~ $re ]] || fail "archive name '$name' does not match <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz"

listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
[[ "$listing" == *"source/data/file1.txt"* ]] || fail "archive is missing source/data/file1.txt"
[[ "$listing" == *"source/file2.txt"* ]] || fail "archive is missing source/file2.txt"
echo "PASS: basic backup"

echo "--- Test 2: rotation with default keep (7) ---"
dest_rot="$tmpdir/backups-rotation"
mkdir -p "$dest_rot"
make_fake_archives "$dest_rot" 1 10

# Stray files that must survive rotation:
#  - inside dest, not matching the archive name pattern
#  - inside dest, a .tar.gz but not matching the timestamp pattern
#  - outside dest, matching the archive name pattern
stray_notes="$dest_rot/notes.txt"
stray_tarball="$dest_rot/source-not-an-archive.tar.gz"
stray_outside="$tmpdir/source-20260115-000000.tar.gz"
echo "keep me" > "$stray_notes"
touch "$stray_tarball"
touch "$stray_outside"

# --keep-weekly 0 isolates the daily rule so this test is correct regardless
# of when it runs (the January fixtures would otherwise be inside the weekly
# window if the suite happened to run in early 2026).
bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_rot"

count=$(count_archives "$dest_rot" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 7 ]] || fail "expected 7 archives after rotation, found $count"

i=1
while (( i <= 10 )); do
  f="$dest_rot/source-202601$(printf '%02d' "$i")-000000.tar.gz"
  if (( i <= 4 )); then
    [[ ! -e "$f" ]] || fail "old archive $f should have been deleted"
  else
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || fail "archive $f should have been kept"
  fi
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done

[[ -e "$stray_notes" ]] || fail "stray file $stray_notes was deleted by rotation"
[[ -e "$stray_tarball" ]] || fail "non-matching file $stray_tarball was deleted by rotation"
[[ -e "$stray_outside" ]] || fail "file outside destination $stray_outside was deleted by rotation"
echo "PASS: rotation keeps the 7 newest (default)"

echo "--- Test 3: rotation with --keep-daily 3 ---"
dest_opt="$tmpdir/backups-keep3"
mkdir -p "$dest_opt"
make_fake_archives "$dest_opt" 1 10

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 3 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_opt"

count=$(count_archives "$dest_opt" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 3 ]] || fail "expected 3 archives after rotation, found $count"
[[ -e "$dest_opt/source-20260109-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "source-20260109-000000.tar.gz should have been kept"
[[ -e "$dest_opt/source-20260110-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "source-20260110-000000.tar.gz should have been kept"
echo "PASS: --keep-daily 3 honored"

echo "--- Test 4: --keep-daily validation ---"
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-daily 0 should have been rejected"
fi
echo "PASS: --keep-daily 0 rejected"

echo "--- Test 5: --help ---"
if ! help_out=$(bash bin/backup.sh --help 2>&1); then
  fail "--help should exit successfully"
fi
[[ "$help_out" == *"Usage:"* ]] || fail "--help output is missing the usage line"
[[ "$help_out" == *"--keep-daily"* ]] || fail "--help output is missing the --keep-daily option"
echo "PASS: --help"

echo "--- Test 6: --verify ---"
dest_verify="$tmpdir/backups-verify"
verify_out="$tmpdir/verify-out.txt"
bash bin/backup.sh --verify "$source_dir" "$dest_verify" > "$verify_out" 2>&1 || fail "--verify run should have succeeded"
grep -q "Verified" "$verify_out" || fail "--verify run did not report verification"

# Force an empty listing: stub tar -tzf to print nothing
real_tar=$(command -v tar)
fakebin="$tmpdir/fakebin"
mkdir -p "$fakebin"
cat > "$fakebin/tar" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [[ \"\$1\" == \"-tzf\" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi
exec \"$real_tar\" \"\$@\"
EOF
chmod +x "$fakebin/tar"

if PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" bash bin/backup.sh --verify "$source_dir" "$dest_verify" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--verify should fail when the listing is empty"
fi
echo "PASS: --verify"

echo "--- Test 7: --exclude (repeatable) ---"
source_excl="$tmpdir/source-excl"
mkdir -p "$source_excl/.cache"
echo "important" > "$source_excl/data.txt"
echo "note" > "$source_excl/notes.tmp"
echo "junk" > "$source_excl/.cache/tmp.bin"

# Control run: without --exclude, .cache must be in the archive
dest_excl_all="$tmpdir/backups-excl-all"
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_excl" "$dest_excl_all" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "control run without --exclude failed"
mapfile -t archives_all < <(find "$dest_excl_all" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' | sort -r)
listing_all=$(tar -tzf "${archives_all[0]}")
[[ "$listing_all" == *".cache"* ]] || fail "control: .cache should be present without --exclude"

# With two --exclude options, both must be absent
dest_excl="$tmpdir/backups-excl"
bash bin/backup.sh --exclude .cache --exclude notes.tmp "$source_excl" "$dest_excl" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "--exclude run failed"
mapfile -t archives_excl < <(find "$dest_excl" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' | sort -r)
[[ ${#archives_excl[@]} -eq 1 ]] || fail "expected 1 archive after --exclude run, found ${#archives_excl[@]}"
listing=$(tar -tzf "${archives_excl[0]}")
if [[ "$listing" == *".cache"* ]]; then
  fail ".cache was not excluded from the archive"
fi
if [[ "$listing" == *"notes.tmp"* ]]; then
  fail "notes.tmp was not excluded from the archive"
fi
[[ "$listing" == *"source-excl/data.txt"* ]] || fail "data.txt missing from excluded-run archive"
echo "PASS: --exclude (repeatable)"

echo "--- Test 8: --dry-run ---"
dest_dry="$tmpdir/backups-dry"
mkdir -p "$dest_dry"
make_fake_archives "$dest_dry" 1 10

dry_out="$tmpdir/dry-out.txt"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_dry" > "$dry_out" 2>&1 || fail "--dry-run should succeed"

# every output line must start with DRY:
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [[ "$line" == "DRY:"* ]] || fail "dry-run line does not start with 'DRY:' -> $line"
done < "$dry_out"

grep -q "^DRY: would create: $dest_dry/source-[0-9]\{8\}-[0-9]\{6\}\.tar\.gz$" "$dry_out" \
  || fail "missing DRY create line for the new archive"

del_count=$(grep -c "^DRY: would delete: " "$dry_out" || true)
# 10 existing + 1 to-be-created = 11, keep 7 => 4 oldest would be deleted
[[ "$del_count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 DRY delete lines, got $del_count"

# nothing was touched: all 10 fakes remain, no new archive was created
count=$(count_archives "$dest_dry" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 10 ]] || fail "dry-run changed the archive count: $count"

# a missing destination directory is not created either
dest_dry_new="$tmpdir/backups-dry-new"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dry_new" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "--dry-run with missing dest should succeed"
[[ ! -e "$dest_dry_new" ]] || fail "dry-run created the destination directory"
echo "PASS: --dry-run"

echo "--- Test 9: missing source directory ---"
missing_src="$tmpdir/does-not-exist"
missing_out="$tmpdir/missing-out.txt"
missing_err="$tmpdir/missing-err.txt"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$missing_src" "$dest_dir" > "$missing_out" 2> "$missing_err"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected exit 2 for missing source, got $rc"
grep -q "source directory" "$missing_err" || fail "stderr does not mention the missing source directory"
[[ ! -s "$missing_out" ]] || fail "expected no stdout output for missing source"
echo "PASS: missing source exits 2"

# 10. Locking: while another process holds the destination lock, a second run
#     exits 3 with a clear message and creates nothing; once the holder
#     releases, a normal run succeeds. The test holds the same lock file the
#     script uses, so the contention is deterministic (no timing dependence).
echo "--- Test 10: lock file prevents concurrent runs ---"
dest_lock="$tmpdir/backups-lock"
mkdir -p "$dest_lock"
make_fake_archives "$dest_lock" 1 3

lockfile="$dest_lock/backup-source.lock"

if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # Hold the lock for 5 seconds; flock releases it when the command exits.
  flock "$lockfile" -c 'sleep 5' &
  holder=$!
  # Wait until the holder actually holds it. The probe only briefly grabs the
  # lock while it is free, and nothing else contends during this window.
  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 100; attempt++ )); do
    if ! flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.1
  done
else
  # No flock: emulate the fallback protocol with a pidfile holding a live pid;
  # the script must treat it as a held lock.
  sleep 5 &
  holder=$!
  printf '%s\n' "$holder" > "$lockfile"
  sleep 0.2
fi

lock_out2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.out"
lock_err2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.err"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out2" 2> "$lock_err2"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]] || fail "second concurrent run should exit 3, got $rc"
grep -qi "lock" "$lock_err2" || fail "stderr of the locked-out run does not mention the lock: $(cat "$lock_err2")"
[[ -z "$(cat "$lock_out2")" ]] || fail "locked-out run printed to stdout"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 3 ]] || fail "locked-out run changed the archive count: $count"

# Once the holder releases, a normal run succeeds and creates its archive.
wait "$holder" || fail "lock holder should have exited"
lock_out3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.out"
lock_err3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.err"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out3" 2> "$lock_err3"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || fail "run after lock release should succeed, got $rc (stderr: $(cat "$lock_err3"))"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after released run (3 fakes + new), got $count"
echo "PASS: lock file prevents concurrent runs (exit 3)"

# 11. Weekly retention: the keep set is the union of (a) the --keep-daily
#     newest archives and (b) the newest archive of each of the last N ISO
#     weeks. Fixtures span the five most recent weeks so that some are kept
#     only by the weekly rule and some are deleted because they are neither in
#     the daily set nor the latest of their week.
echo "--- Test 11: --keep-weekly retention (union with --keep-daily) ---"
dest_wk="$tmpdir/backups-weekly"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk"
w00=$(week_date 0 0)  # this week, Monday         -> kept (daily set)
w11=$(week_date 1 1)  # last week, Tuesday         -> deleted (not latest in its week)
w12=$(week_date 1 2)  # last week, Wednesday       -> kept (weekly: latest of last week)
w21=$(week_date 2 1)  # 2 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> kept (weekly: latest of that week)
w31=$(week_date 3 1)  # 3 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> deleted (outside weekly window)
w41=$(week_date 4 1)  # 4 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> deleted (outside weekly window)
for n in "$w00" "$w11" "$w12" "$w21" "$w31" "$w41"; do
  touch "$dest_wk/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 3 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk"

[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w00}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w00 (in the daily set) should be kept"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w12}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w12 (latest of last week) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w21}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w21 (latest of 2-weeks-ago) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w11}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w11 (not latest in its week, outside daily set) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w31}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w31 (outside the weekly window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w41}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w41 (outside the weekly window) should be deleted"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk" source)
# Kept: the new archive + w00 + w12 + w21 = 4; deleted: w11 + w31 + w41.
[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after weekly rotation, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly retention (union with --keep-daily)"

# 12. --keep-weekly 0: the weekly rule is off, so only the daily set survives.
echo "--- Test 12: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention ---"
dest_wk0="$tmpdir/backups-weekly0"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk0"
for n in "$w00" "$w11" "$w12" "$w21" "$w31" "$w41"; do
  touch "$dest_wk0/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk0"

# Only the 2 newest survive: the new archive + w00. The weekly-kept fakes
# (w12, w21) are now deleted, proving the weekly rule is disabled.
[[ -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w00}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w00 should be kept by the daily rule"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w12}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w12 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w21}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w21 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk0" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected 2 archives with weekly disabled, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention"

# 13. --keep-weekly validation: 0 and positive integers are accepted; negative
#     and non-numeric values are rejected with exit 2.
echo "--- Test 13: --keep-weekly validation ---"
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly -1 "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly -1 should have been rejected"
fi
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly abc "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly abc should have been rejected"
fi
if ! bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly 0 should be accepted"
fi
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly validation"

echo "PASS: all tests passed"

## Summary

**`bin/backup.sh`** — added `--keep-weekly N` (default 4, 0 disables):
- **`iso_week_index()`** — monotonic ISO-week integer = `monday_epoch / 604800`. Consecutive weeks always differ by exactly 1 across year boundaries and 53-week years (avoids `%V`/`%G` wraparound).
- **`rotate_old_archives()`** now builds a single `keep_set` associative array = **union** of:
  - the `--keep-daily` newest archives (threshold shifted by `incoming` for dry-run), and
  - the newest archive of each ISO week in `[now−N+1, now]` (newest-first scan + `seen_week` dedup).

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- All dry-run output lines must start with `DRY:` (enforced in test)
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.
- `--keep-weekly` accepts non-negative integer (0 disables weekly retention); validated with `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`
- Weekly retention uses ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), anchored to current UTC week inclusive
- `iso_week_index` must be monotonic across year boundaries (use `monday_epoch / 604800`, not `%V`/`%G`)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are basenames from a flat-dir glob; every `rm` re-anchors to `"${dest%/}/$b"`.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative.
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: Catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: Matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree.
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (for existing tests): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07).
- **Contents check via variable capture**: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: Fake `tar` intercepts `-tzf`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: not-a-tar.gz, tar.gz-but-wrong-pattern, outside-dest.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter**: Shifts keep threshold so dry-run report matches real-run behavior.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" includes the destination directory.
- **Exit code 2 for missing source**: Consistent with all other argument/validation errors.
- **Lock file naming: `backup-<base>.lock`** (per-source, not per-dest): Allows different sources backing up to the same destination to run in parallel.
- **Lock acquired after `mkdir -p "$dest"` and before any mutation**: Ordering ensures the dest exists for the lock file.
- **flock preferred, noclobber pidfile fallback**: flock auto-releases on process exit; noclobber writes `$$` and checks liveness.
- **Dry-run takes no lock**: Acquiring a lock requires creating the lock file, which would violate "don't touch anything."
- **`flock -n <fd>` vs `flock -n <file> -c true`**: Use file mode for non-destructive probes.

edits.oldText:
#   11. --keep-weekly retention: the keep set is the union of the daily keep
#        set and the newest archive of each of the last N ISO weeks
edits.newText:
#   11. --keep-weekly retention across six weeks: the keep set is the union of

edits.oldText:
# 11. Weekly retention: the keep set is the union of (a) the --keep-daily
#     newest archives and (b) the newest archive of each of the last N ISO
#     weeks. Fixtures span the five most recent weeks so that some are kept
#     only by the weekly rule and some are deleted because they are neither in
#     the daily set nor the latest of their week.
echo "--- Test 11: --keep-weekly retention (union with --keep-daily) ---"
dest_wk="$tmpdir/backups-weekly"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk"
w00=$(week_date 0 0)  # this week, Monday         -> kept (daily set)
w11=$(week_date 1 1)  # last week, Tuesday         -> deleted (not latest in its week)
w12=$(week_date 1 2)  # last week, Wednesday       -> kept (weekly: latest of last week)
w21=$(week_date 2 1)  # 2 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> kept (weekly: latest of that week)
w31=$(week_date 3 1)  # 3 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> deleted (outside weekly window)
w41=$(week_date 4 1)  # 4 weeks ago, Tuesday       -> deleted (outside weekly window)
for n in "$w00" "$w11" "$w12" "$w21" "$w31" "$w41"; do
  touch "$dest_wk/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 3 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk"

[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w00}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w00 (in the daily set) should be kept"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w12}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w12 (latest of last week) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w21}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w21 (latest of 2-weeks-ago) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w11}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w11 (not latest in its week, outside daily set) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w31}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w31 (outside the weekly window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w41}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w41 (outside the weekly window) should be deleted"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk" source)
# Kept: the new archive + w00 + w12 + w21 = 4; deleted: w11 + w31 + w41.
[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after weekly rotation, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly retention (union with --keep-daily)"
edits.newText:
# 11. Weekly retention across six ISO weeks. The keep set is the union of
#     (a) the --keep-daily newest archives and (b) the newest archive of each
#     of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks (window [now-N+1, now]). The fixtures
#     are spread over six weeks, with several archives in some weeks, so the
#     test reaches every branch of the policy: a daily-only survivor, weekly-only
#     survivors in three different in-window weeks, the oldest week still inside
#     the window (inclusive edge), a week just outside the window, and non-newest
#     archives inside in-window weeks.
#     keep_daily=2 keeps {new archive, w0a}; keep_weekly=4 covers weeks
#     W0..W-3, so the newest of W-1 / W-2 / W-3 also survives.
echo "--- Test 11: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks ---"
dest_wk="$tmpdir/backups-weekly"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk"
# Fakes are stamped at 00:00:00 so the real archive (created now) is always the
# newest in the current week. Only day 0 is used in the current week so it can
# never be in the future, regardless of what day of the week the suite runs on.
w0a=$(week_date 0 0)   # W0  Mon  -> kept by DAILY only (the real archive is W0's newest)
w1a=$(week_date 1 0)   # W-1 Mon  -> deleted (not the newest of W-1)
w1b=$(week_date 1 4)   # W-1 Fri  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-1)
w2a=$(week_date 2 1)   # W-2 Tue  -> deleted (not the newest of W-2)
w2b=$(week_date 2 5)   # W-2 Sat  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-2)
w3=$(week_date 3 2)    # W-3 Wed  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-3, oldest week in window)
w4=$(week_date 4 3)    # W-4 Thu  -> deleted (just outside the window)
w5a=$(week_date 5 1)   # W-5 Tue  -> deleted (outside the window)
w5b=$(week_date 5 5)   # W-5 Sat  -> deleted (outside the window)
for n in "$w0a" "$w1a" "$w1b" "$w2a" "$w2b" "$w3" "$w4" "$w5a" "$w5b"; do
  touch "$dest_wk/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 4 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk"

# Daily-only survivor: the real archive is the newest of W0, so the weekly rule
# keeps the real one (not w0a); w0a survives solely via the daily rule.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a (daily-only survivor) should be kept"
# Weekly-only survivors: the newest archive of each in-window week.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b (newest of W-1) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b (newest of W-2) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 (newest of W-3, window edge) should be kept by the weekly rule"
# Non-newest archives inside in-window weeks are deleted.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1a (not newest of W-1) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2a (not newest of W-2) should be deleted"
# Weeks outside the weekly window are deleted (none of them are in the daily set).
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w4}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w4 (W-4, just outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5a (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5b (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk" source)
# Kept: new archive + w0a + w1b + w2b + w3 = 5; deleted: w1a w2a w4 w5a w5b.
[[ "$count" -eq 5 ]] || fail "expected 5 archives after six-week rotation, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks"

edits.oldText:
# 12. --keep-weekly 0: the weekly rule is off, so only the daily set survives.
echo "--- Test 12: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention ---"
dest_wk0="$tmpdir/backups-weekly0"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk0"
for n in "$w00" "$w11" "$w12" "$w21" "$w31" "$w41"; do
  touch "$dest_wk0/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk0"

# Only the 2 newest survive: the new archive + w00. The weekly-kept fakes
# (w12, w21) are now deleted, proving the weekly rule is disabled.
[[ -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w00}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w00 should be kept by the daily rule"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w12}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w12 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w21}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w21 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk0" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected 2 archives with weekly disabled, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention"
edits.newText:
# 12. --keep-weekly 0: with the same six-week fixtures, the weekly rule is off,
#     so only the daily set survives. The archives that test 11 kept purely by

done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk0"

# Only the 2 newest survive: the new archive + w0a.
[[ -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a should be kept by the daily rule"
# The weekly-only survivors from test 11 are now gone, proving the weekly
# rule is disabled.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk0" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected 2 archives with weekly disabled, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify]
#                   [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run]
#                   <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        retention counts: --keep-daily (default 7) and --keep-weekly
#            (default 4); see --help
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (every such line
#   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered. The keep set is the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
# and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks
# (Mon-Sun); everything else is deleted. Nothing outside <destination-dir>
# is ever touched.
#
# Concurrency: each run holds an exclusive lock on
# <destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock for the whole
# create+rotate (flock(1) when available, else a noclobber pidfile);
# a second concurrent run exits 3. --dry-run takes no lock.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate out
older archives. Retention keeps the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep (default: 7)
  --keep-weekly N  Additionally keep the newest archive from each of the last
                   N ISO weeks (Mon-Sun), counted back from the current UTC
                   week inclusive; 0 disables it (default: 4)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (each line
                   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit

}

# Monotonic integer index of the ISO week (Mon-Sun) that contains YYYYMMDD:
# (epoch of that week's Monday, UTC) / 604800. Consecutive ISO weeks differ by
# exactly 1 regardless of the year, leap weeks (53), or the Jan-1/Dec-31
# boundary — unlike %V/%G, which wrap around year edges.
iso_week_index() {
  local d="$1"
  local dash="${d:0:4}-${d:4:2}-${d:6:2}"
  local out epoch dow mon
  out=$(date -u -d "$dash" '+%s %u')
  epoch=${out%% *}
  dow=${out##* }
  mon=$(( epoch - (dow - 1) * 86400 ))
  echo $(( mon / 604800 ))
}

# Delete the oldest archives in $1 beyond the retention policy. Candidates are
# basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz,
# and deletions are always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 is ever
# removed. The keep set is the union of (a) the newest $3 archives and (b) the
# newest archive of each of the last $5 ISO weeks (0 disables it).
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives a real run would
# add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the daily keep threshold so
# the dry report matches a real run. Weekly retention is anchored to the
# current UTC week, which an incoming archive cannot move, so it is not shifted.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}" keep_weekly="${5:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)

  # Build the keep set (basenames) from both retention rules.
  local -A keep_set=()
  i=0
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming < keep )); then
      keep_set["$b"]=1
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"

  if (( keep_weekly > 0 )); then
    local now_week min_week
    now_week=$(iso_week_index "$(date -u +%Y%m%d)")
    min_week=$(( now_week - keep_weekly + 1 ))
    local -A seen_week=()
    local stem date8 wk
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r b; do
      stem="${b#"$base"-}"
      date8="${stem:0:8}"
      wk=$(iso_week_index "$date8")
      # Scanning newest-first, the first archive seen for a week is its newest.
      if (( wk >= min_week && wk <= now_week )) && [[ -z "${seen_week[$wk]:-}" ]]; then
        keep_set["$b"]=1
        seen_week["$wk"]=1
      fi
      i=$(( i + 1 ))
    done <<< "$sorted"
  fi

  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if [[ -z "${keep_set[$b]:-}" ]]; then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        echo "DRY: would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        echo "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_weekly=4

  lock_use_flock=0

    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT

    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else

      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2

        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi

  # inside the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
  tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")

      tar_args+=(--exclude "$pattern")
    done
  fi
  tar_args+=("$base")
  tar "${tar_args[@]}"

  if (( verify )); then
    listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
    if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
      echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
  fi

fi

- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- All dry-run output lines must start with `DRY:` (enforced in test)
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.
- `--keep-weekly` accepts non-negative integer (0 disables weekly retention); validated with `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`
- Weekly retention uses ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), anchored to current UTC week inclusive
- `iso_week_index` must be monotonic across year boundaries (use `monday_epoch / 604800`, not `%V`/`%G`)

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are basenames from a flat-dir glob; every `rm` re-anchors to `"${dest%/}/$b"`.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative.
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: Catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: Matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree.
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (for existing tests): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07).
- **Contents check via variable capture**: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: Fake `tar` intercepts `-tzf`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: not-a-tar.gz, tar.gz-but-wrong-pattern, outside-dest.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter**: Shifts keep threshold so dry-run report matches real-run behavior.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" includes the destination directory.
- **Exit code 2 for missing source**: Consistent with all other argument/validation errors.
- **Lock file naming: `backup-<base>.lock`** (per-source, not per-dest): Allows different sources backing up to the same destination to run in parallel.
- **Lock acquired after `mkdir -p "$dest"` and before any mutation**: Ordering ensures the dest exists for the lock file.
- **flock preferred, noclobber pidfile fallback**: flock auto-releases on process exit; noclobber writes `$$` and checks liveness.
- **Dry-run takes no lock**: Acquiring a lock requires creating the lock file, which would violate "don't touch anything."
- **`flock -n <fd>` vs `flock -n <file> -c true`**: Use file mode for non-destructive probes.
- **Test suite uses fail-fast `fail` guards**, not a pass counter.
- **ISO week index = `monday_epoch / 604800`**: Strictly monotonic integer per ISO week; avoids `%V`/`%G` year-boundary wrap.
- **Weekly retention keep-set**: For each ISO week in `[now_week - keep_weekly + 1, now_week]`, keep the newest archive in that week. Scanning `sorted` (newest-first), the first hit per week is its newest. Uses `declare -A seen_week=()` to track which weeks are already represented.
- **Keep-set is an associative array** (`local -A keep_set=()`): Final deletion loop skips any candidate whose basename is in `keep_set`. Union of daily + weekly is computed by populating the same associative array.
- **Early return `total <= keep_daily → return 0`** remains valid with weekly retention: if all candidates fit in the daily window, weekly retention (a subset) adds no new keeps, so nothing is deleted.
- **`incoming` does NOT shift weekly retention**: The latest archive in the current week is at rank 0. Past weeks are unaffected.
- **`--keep-weekly` validation**: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` — allows 0 (disables), rejects negatives and non-numeric. Exit 2 on failure.
- **Test fixture dates generated relative to current ISO week** (not hardcoded): Use a `week_date weeks_back day_offset` helper. Makes tests robust to any run date.
- **W0 fakes only on day 0 (Monday)**: Ensures the fake is never in the future relative to the real archive, regardless of what day of the week the suite runs on.
- **Test 11 six-week design** (keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=4, window W0–W-3): Fakes: w0a(W0 Mon), w1a(W-1 Mon), w1b(W-1 Fri), w2a(W-2 Tue), w2b(W-2 Sat), w3(W-3 Wed), w4(W-4 Thu), w5a(W-5 Tue), w5b(W-5 Sat). Kept: real+w0a(daily)+w1b(weekly W-1)+w2b(weekly W-2)+w3(weekly W-3, edge)=5. Deleted: w1a,w2a,w4,w5a,w5b=5.
- **Test 12 six-week design** (keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=0): Same fixtures, weekly disabled. Only {real, w0a} retained (2 archives). Proves w1b, w2b, w3 (weekly-only from test 11) are deleted.

- **Date extraction from basename**: `stem="${b#"$base"-}"` then `date8="${stem:0:8}"` (not `${b:0:8}` which would include the prefix).
- **Existing test suite base is "source"**: `source_dir="$tmpdir/source"` so `make_fake_archives` naming `source-*` correctly matches.
- **Daily-only tests pin `--keep-weekly 0`**: Tests 2, 3, and 8 explicitly disable weekly retention so their assertions about daily rotation are correct regardless of when the suite runs.

[[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]] || fail "second concurrent run should exit 3, got $rc"
grep -qi "lock" "$lock_err2" || fail "stderr of the locked-out run does not mention the lock: $(cat "$lock_err2")"
[[ -z "$(cat "$lock_out2")" ]] || fail "locked-out run printed to stdout"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 3 ]] || fail "locked-out run changed the archive count: $count"

# Once the holder releases, a normal run succeeds and creates its archive.
wait "$holder" || fail "lock holder should have exited"
lock_out3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.out"
lock_err3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.err"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out3" 2> "$lock_err3"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || fail "run after lock release should succeed, got $rc (stderr: $(cat "$lock_err3"))"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after released run (3 fakes + new), got $count"
echo "PASS: lock file prevents concurrent runs (exit 3)"

# 11. Weekly retention across six ISO weeks. The keep set is the union of
#     (a) the --keep-daily newest archives and (b) the newest archive of each
#     of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks (window [now-N+1, now]). The fixtures
#     are spread over six weeks, with several archives in some weeks, so the
#     test reaches every branch of the policy: a daily-only survivor, weekly-only
#     survivors in three different in-window weeks, the oldest week still inside
#     the window (inclusive edge), a week just outside the window, and non-newest
#     archives inside in-window weeks.
#     keep_daily=2 keeps {new archive, w0a}; keep_weekly=4 covers weeks
#     W0..W-3, so the newest of W-1 / W-2 / W-3 also survives.
echo "--- Test 11: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks ---"
dest_wk="$tmpdir/backups-weekly"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk"
# Fakes are stamped at 00:00:00 so the real archive (created now) is always the
# newest in the current week. Only day 0 is used in the current week so it can
# never be in the future, regardless of what day of the week the suite runs on.
w0a=$(week_date 0 0)   # W0  Mon  -> kept by DAILY only (the real archive is W0's newest)
w1a=$(week_date 1 0)   # W-1 Mon  -> deleted (not the newest of W-1)
w1b=$(week_date 1 4)   # W-1 Fri  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-1)
w2a=$(week_date 2 1)   # W-2 Tue  -> deleted (not the newest of W-2)
w2b=$(week_date 2 5)   # W-2 Sat  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-2)
w3=$(week_date 3 2)    # W-3 Wed  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-3, oldest week in window)
w4=$(week_date 4 3)    # W-4 Thu  -> deleted (just outside the window)
w5a=$(week_date 5 1)   # W-5 Tue  -> deleted (outside the window)
w5b=$(week_date 5 5)   # W-5 Sat  -> deleted (outside the window)
for n in "$w0a" "$w1a" "$w1b" "$w2a" "$w2b" "$w3" "$w4" "$w5a" "$w5b"; do
  touch "$dest_wk/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 4 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk"

# Daily-only survivor: the real archive is the newest of W0, so the weekly rule
# keeps the real one (not w0a); w0a survives solely via the daily rule.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a (daily-only survivor) should be kept"
# Weekly-only survivors: the newest archive of each in-window week.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b (newest of W-1) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b (newest of W-2) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 (newest of W-3, window edge) should be kept by the weekly rule"
# Non-newest archives inside in-window weeks are deleted.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1a (not newest of W-1) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2a (not newest of W-2) should be deleted"
# Weeks outside the weekly window are deleted (none of them are in the daily set).
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w4}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w4 (W-4, just outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5a (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5b (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk" source)
# Kept: new archive + w0a + w1b + w2b + w3 = 5; deleted: w1a w2a w4 w5a w5b.
[[ "$count" -eq 5 ]] || fail "expected 5 archives after six-week rotation, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks"

# 12. --keep-weekly 0: with the same six-week fixtures, the weekly rule is off,
#     so only the daily set survives. The archives that test 11 kept purely by
#     the weekly rule (w1b, w2b, w3) must now be deleted.
echo "--- Test 12: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention ---"
dest_wk0="$tmpdir/backups-weekly0"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk0"
for n in "$w0a" "$w1a" "$w1b" "$w2a" "$w2b" "$w3" "$w4" "$w5a" "$w5b"; do
  touch "$dest_wk0/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk0"

# Only the 2 newest survive: the new archive + w0a.
[[ -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a should be kept by the daily rule"
# The weekly-only survivors from test 11 are now gone, proving the weekly
# rule is disabled.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk0" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected 2 archives with weekly disabled, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention"

# 13. --keep-weekly validation: 0 and positive integers are accepted; negative
#     and non-numeric values are rejected with exit 2.
echo "--- Test 13: --keep-weekly validation ---"
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly -1 "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly -1 should have been rejected"
fi
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly abc "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly abc should have been rejected"
fi
if ! bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly 0 should be accepted"
fi
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly validation"

echo "PASS: all tests passed"

content.text:
Done. Added a `--quiet` option to `bin/backup.sh`.

**How it works:**
- The informational **stdout** messages — `Created …`, `Removing old archive: …`, `Verified …`, and the dry-run `DRY:` lines — now go through a small `log()` helper that only prints when `--quiet` is off:
  ```bash
  log() {
    if (( ! quiet )); then
      echo "$@"
    fi
  }
  ```
- **Errors were already on stderr** and are untouched, so a quiet run still reports failures (missing source, validation errors, lock contention, verification failure) and exits with the right code.
- `--help` is unaffected (an explicit request still prints).

**Scope decision:** `--quiet` suppresses stdout only. The one stderr `Warning:` (stale-lock takeover) is left as-is since it's on the error stream — "errors and nothing else" is satisfied with no change to error behavior.

**Also updated:**
- Header comment, `usage()`, and `help()` all document `--quiet`.
- New **test 14** verifies: a quiet success prints empty stdout but still writes the archive; a quiet `--dry-run` prints nothing; a quiet argument error still writes `Error…` to stderr with empty stdout.

**Verification:** ShellCheck clean on both files; full suite **14/14 pass**; manual run confirmed a quiet run is silent on stdout while the archive is still created and errors still surface on stderr. Committed as `3cbb797`.

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- All dry-run output lines must start with `DRY:` (enforced in test)
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.
- `--keep-weekly` accepts non-negative integer (0 disables weekly retention); validated with `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`
- Weekly retention uses ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), anchored to current UTC week inclusive
- `iso_week_index` must be monotonic across year boundaries (use `monday_epoch / 604800`, not `%V`/`%G`)

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates as basenames, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N, all deletions re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"`
- [x] `--verify` flag — after writing, runs `tar -tzf "$archive"`; fails (exit 1) if listing is empty; verified **before** rotation
- [x] `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable, also `--exclude=PATTERN`) — patterns passed to tar as `--exclude`; empty patterns rejected (exit 2); built into a `tar_args` array
- [x] `--dry-run` flag — prints `DRY: would create:` and `DRY: would delete:` lines; skips mkdir, tar, verify, rm
- [x] Missing source directory exits with code **2**, error to stderr
- [x] Lock file implementation in `bin/backup.sh` (flock + noclobber pidfile fallback, stale-lock detection, dry-run skips lock)
- [x] Test 10 rewritten with deterministic flock-based lock holding
- [x] E2E verification: two real runs contend correctly
- [x] Fallback (no-flock) path verified end-to-end

- [x] `iso_week_index` function: computes `monday_epoch / 604800`, gives monotonic values
- [x] Bash version confirmed: 5.3.9, `local -A` associative arrays work

Expected: 5 kept, 5 deleted.

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are basenames from a flat-dir glob; every `rm` re-anchors to `"${dest%/}/$b"`.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative.
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: Catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: Matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree.
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (for existing tests): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07).
- **Contents check via variable capture**: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: Fake `tar` intercepts `-tzf`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` on error prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: not-a-tar.gz, tar.gz-but-wrong-pattern, outside-dest.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter**: Shifts keep threshold so dry-run report matches real-run behavior.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" includes the destination directory.
- **Exit code 2 for missing source**: Consistent with all other argument/validation errors.
- **Lock file naming: `backup-<base>.lock`** (per-source, not per-dest): Allows different sources backing up to the same destination to run in parallel.
- **Lock acquired after `mkdir -p "$dest"` and before any mutation**: Ordering ensures the dest exists for the lock file.
- **flock preferred, noclobber pidfile fallback**: flock auto-releases on process exit; noclobber writes `$$` and checks liveness.
- **Dry-run takes no lock**: Acquiring a lock requires creating the lock file, which would violate "don't touch anything."
- **`flock -n <fd>` vs `flock -n <file> -c true`**: Use file mode for non-destructive probes.
- **Test suite uses fail-fast `fail` guards**, not a pass counter.
- **ISO week index = `monday_epoch / 604800`**: Strictly monotonic integer per ISO week; avoids `%V`/`%G` year-boundary wrap.
- **Weekly retention keep-set**: For each ISO week in `[now_week - keep_weekly + 1, now_week]`, keep the newest archive in that week. Scanning `sorted` (newest-first), the first hit per week is its newest. Uses `declare -A seen_week=()` to track which weeks are already represented.
- **Keep-set is an associative array** (`local -A keep_set=()`): Final deletion loop skips any candidate whose basename is in `keep_set`. Union of daily + weekly is computed by populating the same associative array.
- **Early return `total <= keep_daily → return 0`** remains valid with weekly retention: if all candidates fit in the daily window, weekly retention (a subset) adds no new keeps, so nothing is deleted.
- **`incoming` does NOT shift weekly retention**: The latest archive in the current week is at rank 0. Past weeks are unaffected.
- **`--keep-weekly` validation**: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` — allows 0 (disables), rejects negatives and non-numeric. Exit 2 on failure.
- **Test fixture dates generated relative to current ISO week** (not hardcoded): Use a `week_date weeks_back day_offset` helper. Makes tests robust to any run date.
- **W0 fakes only on day 0 (Monday)**: Ensures the fake is never in the future relative to the real archive, regardless of what day of the week the suite runs on.
- **Test 11 six-week design** (keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=4, window W0–W-3): Fakes: w0a(W0 Mon), w1a(W-1 Mon), w1b(W-1 Fri), w2a(W-2 Tue), w2b(W-2 Sat), w3(W-3 Wed), w4(W-4 Thu), w5a(W-5 Tue), w5b(W-5 Sat). arguments.content:
# systemd example: run `backup.sh` daily

Two units that run `bin/backup.sh` once a day via systemd:

| File                 | Role                                                        |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `sh-backup.service`  | One-shot job that runs the script (create archive + rotate) |
| `sh-backup.timer`    | Triggers the service once per day at 03:00 (local time)     |

## 1. Edit the placeholders

Both units use placeholder paths. Replace them with real **absolute** paths:

- `/opt/sh-backup/bin/backup.sh` — where the installed script lives
- `/path/to/source` — the directory to back up
- `/path/to/backups` — where the `.tar.gz` archives are written

You can also append any `backup.sh` flags (see `bin/backup.sh --help`) after
the destination in `ExecStart`, e.g. `--keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --verify`.

Pick a `User=`/`Group=` that can read `<source>` and write `<dest>`, or delete
those lines to run as root.

## 2. Install

```sh
# copy the units (adjust the source dir if your checkout lives elsewhere)
install -m 0644 sh-backup.service /etc/systemd/system/
install -m 0644 sh-backup.timer   /etc/systemd/system/

# edit the placeholders, e.g.:
#   sed -i 's|/path/to/source|/srv/data|; s|/path/to/backups|/var/backups|' /etc/systemd/system/sh-backup.service

# make systemd pick up the new files
systemctl daemon-reload
```

## 3. Enable and verify

```sh
# schedule it (enable) and run the first cycle now (--now)
systemctl enable --now sh-backup.timer

# confirm the timer is armed and when it next fires
systemctl list-timers sh-backup.timer

# watch a real run's output in the journal (stdout/stderr are auto-captured)
journalctl -u sh-backup.service -f
```

## 4. Run it manually (no timer)

```sh
# one-off run as the unit would do it (uses the same User=/flags)
systemctl start sh-backup.service
systemctl status sh-backup.service
journalctl -u sh-backup.service --since "5 min ago"
```

## Notes

- **Timezone:** `OnCalendar` uses the system **local** time. Archive names are
  always UTC, so changing the schedule never changes file names.
- **Concurrent runs:** the script takes a lock file in the destination and exits
  3 if another run holds it, so an overlapping trigger is safe.
- **`--quiet`:** leave it off for a systemd service — the "Created …" /
  "Removing old archive …" lines are useful in the journal. Add `--quiet` to
  `ExecStart` if you want a quieter journal.
- **Catch-up:** `Persistent=true` runs a missed backup once after the machine
  wakes/boots, which is usually what you want for backups.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify]
#                   [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet]
#                   <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        retention counts: --keep-daily (default 7) and --keep-weekly
#            (default 4); see --help
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (every such line
#   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
#
#   --quiet suppresses all informational output (the created/removed/verify
#   lines and dry-run "DRY:" lines); errors still go to stderr
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered. The keep set is the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
# and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks
# (Mon-Sun); everything else is deleted. Nothing outside <destination-dir>
# is ever touched.
#
# Concurrency: each run holds an exclusive lock on
# <destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock for the whole
# create+rotate (flock(1) when available, else a noclobber pidfile);
# a second concurrent run exits 3. --dry-run takes no lock.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate out
older archives. Retention keeps the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep (default: 7)
  --keep-weekly N  Additionally keep the newest archive from each of the last
                   N ISO weeks (Mon-Sun), counted back from the current UTC
                   week inclusive; 0 disables it (default: 4)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (each line
                   starts with "DRY:") without touching anything
  --quiet          Suppress all informational output (created/removed/verify
                   lines and dry-run "DRY:" lines); errors still go to stderr
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Print an informational message to stdout, unless --quiet is set. Errors are
# always printed separately to stderr; this only governs status output.
log() {
  if (( ! quiet )); then
    echo "$@"
  fi
}

# Monotonic integer index of the ISO week (Mon-Sun) that contains YYYYMMDD:
# (epoch of that week's Monday, UTC) / 604800. Consecutive ISO weeks differ by
# exactly 1 regardless of the year, leap weeks (53), or the Jan-1/Dec-31
# boundary — unlike %V/%G, which wrap around year edges.
iso_week_index() {
  local d="$1"
  local dash="${d:0:4}-${d:4:2}-${d:6:2}"
  local out epoch dow mon
  out=$(date -u -d "$dash" '+%s %u')
  epoch=${out%% *}
  dow=${out##* }
  mon=$(( epoch - (dow - 1) * 86400 ))
  echo $(( mon / 604800 ))
}

# Delete the oldest archives in $1 beyond the retention policy. Candidates are
# basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz,
# and deletions are always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 is ever
# removed. The keep set is the union of (a) the newest $3 archives and (b) the
# newest archive of each of the last $5 ISO weeks (0 disables it).
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives a real run would
# add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the daily keep threshold so
# the dry report matches a real run. Weekly retention is anchored to the
# current UTC week, which an incoming archive cannot move, so it is not shifted.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}" keep_weekly="${5:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)

  # Build the keep set (basenames) from both retention rules.
  local -A keep_set=()
  i=0
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming < keep )); then
      keep_set["$b"]=1
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"

  if (( keep_weekly > 0 )); then
    local now_week min_week
    now_week=$(iso_week_index "$(date -u +%Y%m%d)")
    min_week=$(( now_week - keep_weekly + 1 ))
    local -A seen_week=()
    local stem date8 wk
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r b; do
      stem="${b#"$base"-}"
      date8="${stem:0:8}"
      wk=$(iso_week_index "$date8")
      # Scanning newest-first, the first archive seen for a week is its newest.
      if (( wk >= min_week && wk <= now_week )) && [[ -z "${seen_week[$wk]:-}" ]]; then
        keep_set["$b"]=1
        seen_week["$wk"]=1
      fi
      i=$(( i + 1 ))
    done <<< "$sorted"
  fi

  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if [[ -z "${keep_set[$b]:-}" ]]; then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        log "DRY: would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        log "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7
keep_weekly=4
verify=0
excludes=()
dry_run=0
quiet=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --keep-weekly)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-weekly requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_weekly="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-weekly=*)
      keep_weekly="${1#--keep-weekly=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    --exclude)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("$2")
      shift 2
      ;;
    --exclude=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--exclude=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("${1#--exclude=}")
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run)
      dry_run=1
      shift
      ;;
    --quiet)
      quiet=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_weekly" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-weekly must be a non-negative integer (got '$keep_weekly')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi

base=$(basename "$source")

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"

  # Hold an exclusive lock for the rest of the run so two runs cannot
  # rotate at the same time. Prefer flock(1) when available; otherwise
  # fall back to a noclobber pidfile (a stale lock is detected via the
  # recorded pid and taken over). The lock file lives in the

dest_dir="$tmpdir/backups"

fail() {

# Count archives in $1 that match <source basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.
count_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2"
  local n=0 f b
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      n=$(( n + 1 ))
    fi
  done
  printf '%s' "$n"
}

# Create fake "old" archives in $1 named source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz
# for January days $2..$3 (fixed past dates, one file per day).
make_fake_archives() {
  local dest="$1" first="$2" last="$3"
  local i f
  for (( i = first; i <= last; i++ )); do
    f="$dest/source-202601$(printf '%02d' "$i")-000000.tar.gz"

# Compute YYYYMMDD for a date relative to the current ISO week: $1 = number of
# weeks before this week (0 = this week), $2 = day offset into that week
# (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday). Anchoring to the real current week keeps the
# weekly fixtures correct no matter which day of the week the suite runs on.
week_date() {
  local weeks_back="$1" day_offset="$2"
  local dow monday_epoch target
  dow=$(date -u +%u)
  monday_epoch=$(date -u -d "today - $((dow - 1)) days" +%s)
  target=$(( monday_epoch - weeks_back * 7 * 86400 + day_offset * 86400 ))
  date -u -d "@$target" +%Y%m%d
}
