#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify]
#                   [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet]
#                   <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        retention counts: --keep-daily (default 7) and --keep-weekly
#            (default 4); see --help
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (plain "would
#   create: <path>" / "would delete: <path>" lines) without touching anything
#
#   --quiet suppresses all informational output (the created/removed/verify
#   lines and dry-run lines); errors still go to stderr
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered. The keep set is the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
# and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks
# (Mon-Sun); everything else is deleted. Nothing outside <destination-dir>
# is ever touched.
#
# Concurrency: each run holds an exclusive lock on
# <destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock for the whole
# create+rotate (flock(1) when available, else a noclobber pidfile);
# a second concurrent run exits 3. --dry-run takes no lock.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate out
older archives. Retention keeps the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep (default: 7)
  --keep-weekly N  Additionally keep the newest archive from each of the last
                   N ISO weeks (Mon-Sun), counted back from the current UTC
                   week inclusive; 0 disables it (default: 4)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (plain "would
                   create: <path>" / "would delete: <path>" lines) without
                   touching anything
  --quiet          Suppress all informational output (created/removed/verify
                   lines and dry-run lines); errors still go to stderr
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Print an informational message to stdout, unless --quiet is set. Errors are
# always printed separately to stderr; this only governs status output.
log() {
  if (( ! quiet )); then
    echo "$@"
  fi
}

# Monotonic integer index of the ISO week (Mon-Sun) that contains YYYYMMDD:
# (epoch of that week's Monday, UTC) / 604800. Consecutive ISO weeks differ by
# exactly 1 regardless of the year, leap weeks (53), or the Jan-1/Dec-31
# boundary — unlike %V/%G, which wrap around year edges.
iso_week_index() {
  local d="$1"
  local dash="${d:0:4}-${d:4:2}-${d:6:2}"
  local out epoch dow mon
  out=$(date -u -d "$dash" '+%s %u')
  epoch=${out%% *}
  dow=${out##* }
  mon=$(( epoch - (dow - 1) * 86400 ))
  echo $(( mon / 604800 ))
}

# Delete the oldest archives in $1 beyond the retention policy. Candidates are
# basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz,
# and deletions are always re-anchored to $1 — so nothing outside $1 is ever
# removed. The keep set is the union of (a) the newest $3 archives and (b) the
# newest archive of each of the last $5 ISO weeks (0 disables it).
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives a real run would
# add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the daily keep threshold so
# the dry report matches a real run. Weekly retention is anchored to the
# current UTC week, which an incoming archive cannot move, so it is not shifted.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}" keep_weekly="${5:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local f b total i sorted
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      candidates+=("$b")
    fi
  done

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | sort -r)

  # Build the keep set (basenames) from both retention rules.
  local -A keep_set=()
  i=0
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming < keep )); then
      keep_set["$b"]=1
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"

  if (( keep_weekly > 0 )); then
    local now_week min_week
    now_week=$(iso_week_index "$(date -u +%Y%m%d)")
    min_week=$(( now_week - keep_weekly + 1 ))
    local -A seen_week=()
    local stem date8 wk
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r b; do
      stem="${b#"$base"-}"
      date8="${stem:0:8}"
      wk=$(iso_week_index "$date8")
      # Scanning newest-first, the first archive seen for a week is its newest.
      if (( wk >= min_week && wk <= now_week )) && [[ -z "${seen_week[$wk]:-}" ]]; then
        keep_set["$b"]=1
        seen_week["$wk"]=1
      fi
      i=$(( i + 1 ))
    done <<< "$sorted"
  fi

  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if [[ -z "${keep_set[$b]:-}" ]]; then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        log "would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        log "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

keep_daily=7
keep_weekly=4
verify=0
excludes=()
dry_run=0
quiet=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)

      shift
      ;;
    --keep-weekly)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-weekly requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_weekly="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-weekly=*)
      keep_weekly="${1#--keep-weekly=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    --exclude)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("$2")
      shift 2
      ;;
    --exclude=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--exclude=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("${1#--exclude=}")
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run)
      dry_run=1
      shift
      ;;
    --quiet)
      quiet=1
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_weekly" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-weekly must be a non-negative integer (got '$keep_weekly')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" || ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi

base=$(basename "$source")

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"

  # Hold an exclusive lock for the rest of the run so two runs cannot
  # rotate at the same time. Prefer flock(1) when available; otherwise
  # fall back to a noclobber pidfile (a stale lock is detected via the
  # recorded pid and taken over). The lock file lives in the
  # destination and is not a *.tar.gz, so rotation never touches it.
  lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
  lock_acquired=0
  lock_use_flock=0
  cleanup_lock() {
    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else
      holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
      if ! ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi
  fi
fi

stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

if (( dry_run )); then
  # Report what would happen without touching anything (no mkdir, no
  # tar, no rm); incoming=1 accounts for the archive a real run would
  # create first, so the delete report matches a real run.
  log "would create: $archive"
  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 1 "$keep_weekly"
else
  # Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths
  # inside the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
  tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")
  if (( ${#excludes[@]} > 0 )); then
    for pattern in "${excludes[@]}"; do
      tar_args+=(--exclude "$pattern")
    done
  fi
  tar_args+=("$base")
  tar "${tar_args[@]}"

  log "Created $archive"

  if (( verify )); then
    listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
    if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
      echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    log "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
  fi

  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 0 "$keep_weekly"
fi

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--restore DIR`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- `--quiet`: prints errors (stderr) and nothing else to stdout; informational output (Created/Removing/Verified/dry-run lines) suppressed
- `--restore DIR`: extracts the newest matching archive from the destination into DIR, refusing a non-empty target
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)
- Provides systemd timer + service example for daily scheduled runs
- **Write a README.md with every option and an example of each** (current task)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- Dry-run output uses plain `would create: <path>` / `would delete: <path>` lines (no mandatory prefix); the `DRY:` prefix rule has been lifted

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--restore DIR`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- `--quiet`: prints errors (stderr) and nothing else to stdout; informational output (Created/Removing/Verified/dry-run lines) suppressed
- `--restore DIR`: extracts the newest matching archive from the destination into DIR, refusing a non-empty target
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)
- Provides systemd timer + service example for daily scheduled runs
- **Write a README.md with every option and an example of each** (current task)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- Dry-run output uses plain `would create: <path>` / `would delete: <path>` lines (no mandatory prefix); the `DRY:` prefix rule has been lifted
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options, non-empty restore target)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Exit code 1 for runtime failures (no archive to restore, tar extraction failure)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.

arguments.content:
# sh-backup

A small, dependency-light bash tool that backs up a directory into a
destination as timestamped `tar.gz` archives and rotates out the old ones.

- Creates `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` (timestamp in **UTC**)
  inside a destination directory.
- Rotates: keeps the **union** of the `--keep-daily` newest archives and the
  newest archive from each of the last `--keep-weekly` ISO weeks.
- **Never deletes anything outside the destination** — a structural guarantee,
  not an accident (deletions are re-anchored to the destination path).
- Optional integrity check (`--verify`), file exclusion (`--exclude`),
  dry-run (`--dry-run`), quiet mode (`--quiet`), and disaster-recovery
  restore (`--restore`).
- A lock file prevents two runs from rotating at the same time.
- Ships with a test suite and a systemd timer + service example.

## Requirements

- `bash` (>= 4, for associative arrays)
- `tar`, `date` (GNU), `sort`, `mkdir`, `rm`
- `flock` (recommended; a noclobber pidfile fallback is used when absent)

## Quick start

```sh
# Back up /data/mydb into /backups/mydb, keep 7 newest + 4 weekly:
bin/backup.sh /data/mydb /backups/mydb

# Verify the archive and skip a logs directory:
bin/backup.sh --verify --exclude logs /data/mydb /backups/mydb

# See what a run would do without touching anything:
bin/backup.sh --dry-run /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

## Usage

```
bin/backup.sh [OPTIONS] <source-dir> <destination-dir>
```

**Convention:** all options must come *before* the two positional
arguments. Once the parser sees a non-option argument it stops and treats the
rest as `<source-dir>` `<destination-dir>` (exactly two are required).

`<destination-dir>` is created if it does not exist (unless `--dry-run`).

## Options

> Every option below is shown with a concrete example. Options may use the
> space form (`--keep-daily 7`) or the `=` form (`--keep-daily=7`).

### Positional arguments

| Argument          | Meaning                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<source-dir>`    | The directory to back up.                                             |
| `<destination-dir>` | Where archives are written and rotated.                           |

```sh
bin/backup.sh /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

A missing `<source-dir>` is an argument error (exit 2) — **except** in
`--restore` mode, where the source directory need not exist (only its basename
is used to locate the archive).

### `--keep-daily N`

Keep the **N newest** archives (counting from the top of the sorted list).
Default: `7`. Must be a positive integer; `--keep-daily 0` or a non-numeric
value is rejected (exit 2).

```sh
# Keep only the 3 newest archives:
bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 3 /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--keep-weekly N`

In addition to `--keep-daily`, keep the **newest archive from each of the
last N ISO weeks** (Mon–Sun), counted back from the current UTC week
inclusive. `0` disables weekly retention. Default: `4`. Must be a
non-negative integer.

The retention keep-set is the **union** of the daily set and the weekly set,
so an archive is kept if it satisfies *either* rule.

```sh
# Keep the 10 newest archives plus the newest archive from each of the
# last 6 ISO weeks:
bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 10 --keep-weekly 6 /data/mydb /backups/mydb

# Disable weekly retention (pure "keep N newest"):
bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--verify`

After writing the archive, list its contents with `tar -tzf` and fail (exit 1)
if the listing is empty. Verification runs **before** rotation, so a failed
backup does not trigger cleanup.

```sh
# Create, then verify the archive is readable and non-empty:
bin/backup.sh --verify /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--exclude PATTERN`

Exclude files matching `PATTERN` from the archive. The pattern is passed to
`tar` as `--exclude`, which is **unanchored** (it matches the pattern
anywhere in the tree, e.g. a directory named `logs`). May be given multiple
times. An empty pattern is rejected (exit 2).

```sh
# Skip a logs directory and *.tmp files:
bin/backup.sh --exclude logs --exclude '*.tmp' /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--restore DIR`

Restore-only mode: extract the **newest** matching archive from
`<destination-dir>` into `DIR` (creating `DIR` if needed). Because the
archive's top-level entry is the source basename, files land in
`DIR/<source-basename>/...`.

- Refuses a `DIR` that already exists and is **not empty** (exit 2).
- Exits 1 if there is no matching archive to restore.
- Takes **no lock** and creates **no new backup** (it is read-only on the
  destination).
- The `<source-dir>` need not exist (disaster recovery).

```sh
# Recover the latest backup of /data/mydb into a scratch directory:
bin/backup.sh --restore /tmp/recovered /data/mydb /backups/mydb

# Preview a restore without touching anything (see --dry-run):
bin/backup.sh --dry-run --restore /tmp/recovered /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--dry-run`

Print what a run *would* do and touch nothing (no `mkdir`, no `tar`, no `rm`).
Creates no lock. Output is plain:

```
would create: /backups/mydb/mydb-20261007-120000.tar.gz
would delete: /backups/mydb/mydb-20260101-000000.tar.gz
```

For `--restore` it prints `would extract: <archive> into <target>` instead.

```sh
# Report create/delete without making changes:
bin/backup.sh --dry-run /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `--quiet`

Suppress all **informational** output on stdout (created / removed / verify
lines and dry-run lines). **Errors and warnings still go to stderr.**
`--help` is unaffected (an explicit request still prints).

```sh
# Run silently; only problems will be visible:
bin/backup.sh --quiet /data/mydb /backups/mydb
```

### `-h`, `--help`

Print the help text to stdout and exit 0.

```sh
bin/backup.sh --help
```

## Retention model

Retention keeps the **union** of two sets:

1. **Daily:** the `--keep-daily` newest archives (by filename order, which is
   chronological because timestamps are fixed-width UTC).
2. **Weekly:** for each of the last `--keep-weekly` ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), the
   single newest archive that falls in that week.

An archive is deleted only if it is in *neither* set. Example with
`--keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 4`: the 2 newest are kept, and additionally the
newest archive from each of the current week and the 3 preceding ISO weeks is
kept (whichever of those is not already in the daily set).

## Archive naming & layout

- Filename: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz`, timestamp in UTC.
- Paths inside the archive are **relative**, rooted at the source basename:
  `mydb/file.txt`, `mydb/data/file1.txt`, …
- This means a `tar -tzf` listing shows `mydb/...`, and a restore into
  `DIR` produces `DIR/mydb/...`.

## Rotation safety

Rotation only ever considers files **inside `<destination-dir>`** that match
the exact pattern `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` (regex-anchored).
Stray files — anything else in the destination, or matching files outside it —
are never touched. Every deletion is re-anchored to the destination path, so
it is structurally impossible to remove a file outside the destination.

## Locking

Before any mutation, the run takes an exclusive lock on
`<destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock`:

- `flock(1)` is used when available (auto-released on process exit).
- Otherwise a noclobber pidfile is used, with stale-lock detection (a lock
  whose recorded pid is no longer alive is taken over, with a warning).

A second concurrent run on the same destination+source exits **3** with a
clear message. `--dry-run` and `--restore` take no lock.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                              |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success (including a successful `--restore` or `--help`).            |
| 1    | Runtime failure: `--verify` found an empty listing, no archive to restore, or tar extraction failed. |
| 2    | Argument / validation error: missing source, invalid `--keep-daily` / `--keep-weekly`, unknown option, empty `--exclude` / `--restore`, non-empty restore target, too many arguments. |
| 3    | Another run holds the destination lock.                              |

## Scheduling (systemd)

A ready-to-edit daily timer + service is provided in `examples/`:

- `examples/sh-backup.service` — `Type=oneshot`, runs the backup.
- `examples/sh-backup.timer` — daily at 03:00 local, `Persistent=true`.
- `examples/README.md` — install / enable / verify steps.

```sh
# Point the service at a real backup, then enable the timer:
sudo install -m 644 examples/sh-backup.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo install -m 644 examples/sh-backup.timer    /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now sh-backup.timer
```

## Testing

```sh
bash tests/run.sh
```

The suite (15 tests) covers basic backup, daily + weekly retention, stray-file
safety, `--verify`, `--exclude`, `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--restore`, locking
(a contended second run exits 3), and argument validation.

## Project layout

```
bin/backup.sh            The tool.
tests/run.sh             Test suite.
examples/                systemd service + timer + README.
README.md                This file.
```

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--restore DIR`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- `--quiet`: prints errors (stderr) and nothing else to stdout; informational output (Created/Removing/Verified/dry-run lines) suppressed
- `--restore DIR`: extracts the newest matching archive from the destination into DIR, refusing a non-empty target
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)
- Provides systemd timer + service example for daily scheduled runs
- **Write a README.md with every option and an example of each** (current task)

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- Dry-run output uses plain `would create: <path>` / `would delete: <path>` lines (no mandatory prefix); the `DRY:` prefix rule has been lifted
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options, non-empty restore target)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Exit code 1 for runtime failures (no archive to restore, tar extraction failure)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.
- `--keep-weekly` accepts non-negative integer (0 disables weekly retention); validated with `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`
- Weekly retention uses ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), anchored to current UTC week inclusive
- `iso_week_index` must be monotonic across year boundaries (use `monday_epoch / 604800`, not `%V`/`%G`)
- `--quiet` suppresses stdout only; stderr (errors, warnings) always shows
- `--help` is not affected by `--quiet` (explicit request still prints)
- **Argument order: options must come before positionals.** The parser `break`s on the first non-option arg; remaining `$@` must be exactly 2. Positionals-first invocation will fail with usage + exit 2.

## Key Decisions
- **Lexicographic sort = chronological sort**: Fixed-width UTC timestamps mean `sort -r` on filenames gives newest-first order.
- **Rotation scope — structural guarantee**: Candidates are basenames from a flat-dir glob; every `rm` re-anchors to `"${dest%/}/$b"`.
- **`tar -czf` with `-C "$(dirname "$source")"`**: Archives by basename from parent so paths inside are relative.
- **`--verify` uses command substitution under `set -e`**: Catches both empty and unreadable archives.
- **`--verify` runs before rotation**: A failed backup should not trigger cleanup.
- **`--exclude` uses a tar args array**: `tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")` with `--exclude` flags appended.
- **GNU tar `--exclude` is unanchored by default**: Matches the directory wherever it sits in the tree.
- **Test uses separate dest dirs per scenario**: Avoids cross-contamination.
- **Fake archives use January 2026 dates** (for existing tests): Always older than the real archive (current date 2026-10-07).
- **Contents check via variable capture**: Avoids SIGPIPE flakiness under `pipefail`.
- **`--verify` failure test uses a PATH stub**: Fake `tar` intercepts `-tzf`.
- **`--help` prints to stdout, `usage()` prints to stderr**: Standard CLI convention.
- **Stray file test covers three levels**: not-a-tar.gz, tar.gz-but-wrong-pattern, outside-dest.
- **`--dry-run` uses `incoming` parameter**: Shifts keep threshold so dry-run report matches real-run behavior.
- **`--dry-run` skips `mkdir`**: "Don't touch anything" includes the destination directory.
- **Exit code 2 for missing source**: Consistent with all other argument/validation errors.
- **Lock file naming: `backup-<base>.lock`** (per-source, not per-dest): Allows different sources backing up to the same destination to run in parallel.
- **Lock acquired after `mkdir -p "$dest"` and before any mutation**: Ordering ensures the dest exists for the lock file.
- **flock preferred, noclobber pidfile fallback**: flock auto-releases on process exit; noclobber writes `$$` and checks liveness.
- **Dry-run takes no lock**: Acquiring a lock requires creating the lock file, which would violate "don't touch anything."
- **`flock -n <fd>` vs `flock -n <file> -c true`**: Use file mode for non-destructive probes.
- **Test suite uses fail-fast `fail` guards**, not a pass counter.
- **ISO week index = `monday_epoch / 604800`**: Strictly monotonic integer per ISO week; avoids `%V`/`%G` year-boundary wrap.
- **Weekly retention keep-set**: For each ISO week in `[now_week - keep_weekly + 1, now_week]`, keep the newest archive in that week.
- **Keep-set is an associative array** (`local -A keep_set=()`): Final deletion loop skips any candidate whose basename is in `keep_set`.
- **Early return `total <= keep_daily → return 0`** remains valid with weekly retention.
- **`incoming` does NOT shift weekly retention**.
- **`--keep-weekly` validation**: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` — allows 0 (disables), rejects negatives and non-numeric.
- **Test fixture dates generated relative to current ISO week** (not hardcoded).
- **W0 fakes only on day 0 (Monday)**: Ensures the fake is never in the future relative to the real archive.
- **Test 11 six-week design** (keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=4): 5 kept, 5 deleted.
- **Test 12 six-week design** (keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=0): 2 kept.
- **Test 13 design**: `--keep-weekly` validation.
- **Date extraction from basename**: `stem="${b#"$base"-}"` then `date8="${stem:0:8}"`.
- **Existing test suite base is "source"**: `source_dir="$tmpdir/source"`.
- **Daily-only tests pin `--keep-weekly 0`**: Tests 2, 3, and 8.
- **`--quiet` suppresses stdout only**: The `log()` helper gates stdout informational messages.
- **Stale-lock warning left on stderr, not converted to `log`**.
- **`log()` uses `(( ! quiet ))` in an `if` condition**: Safe under `set -e`.
- **`--help` not affected by `--quiet`**.
- **systemd service uses `Type=oneshot`**.
- **`Persistent=true` on the timer**.
- **`OnCalendar` uses system local time**.
- **Placeholder style for systemd examples**.
- **Daily vs. weekly parsing divergence**: Daily uses lexicographic sort; weekly parses the date.
- **DRY: prefix rule lifted**: Plain output, test 8 updated, `log()` gating preserved.
- **`--restore` does NOT take the backup lock**: Read-only on destination; avoids blocking backups during long extraction. Worst case: archive rotated away mid-extract → tar fails → exit 1.
- **`--restore` source dir need not exist**: Restore is for disaster recovery when the source is gone. Only its basename is used for archive pattern matching.
- **`--restore` target validation order**: (1) find newest archive (exit 1 if none), (2) exists-and-not-a-dir → exit 2, (3) dir-and-non-empty → exit 2, (4) proceed. Archive-finding precedes target validation so the would-extract line is always backed by a real archive.
- **`list_archives` helper** (renamed from `archive_candidates`): Single source of truth for the archive-matching pattern; shared by both `rotate_old_archives` and `do_restore` to guarantee they agree on what counts as "our" archives. Takes `dest` and `base`, prints matching basenames one per line.
- **Newest selection via `${newest%%$'\n'*}`**: Avoids `head -n1` SIGPIPE under `pipefail`. Takes first *line* (not first space-delimited token) to handle basenames with spaces.
- **`find -mindepth 1 -print -quit` for non-empty check**: Handles dotfiles; `-quit` stops at first entry (efficient); `find` confirmed available at `/usr/bin/find`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# backup.sh — create a timestamped tar.gz backup of a source directory,
# then rotate out old archives.
#
# Usage: backup.sh [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify]
#                   [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet]
#                   <source-dir> <destination-dir>
#
#   N        retention counts: --keep-daily (default 7) and --keep-weekly
#            (default 4); see --help
#   PATTERN  excluded from the archive, passed to tar as --exclude;
#            may be given multiple times
#
#   --dry-run prints what would be created and deleted (plain "would
#   create: <path>" / "would delete: <path>" lines) without touching anything
#
#   --quiet suppresses all informational output (the created/removed/verify
#   lines and dry-run lines); errors still go to stderr
#
# The archive is written into <destination-dir> as
#   <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz  (timestamp in UTC)
#
# Rotation: after creating the new archive, only files inside
# <destination-dir> whose names match the pattern for this source are
# considered. The keep set is the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
# and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks
# (Mon-Sun); everything else is deleted. Nothing outside <destination-dir>
# is ever touched.
#
# Concurrency: each run holds an exclusive lock on
# <destination-dir>/backup-<source-basename>.lock for the whole
# create+rotate (flock(1) when available, else a noclobber pidfile);
# a second concurrent run exits 3. --dry-run takes no lock.
#
# Restore: --restore DIR runs restore-only mode — it extracts the newest
# matching archive from <destination-dir> into DIR (creating DIR if needed),
# refusing a DIR that exists and is non-empty. No new backup is created and no
# lock is taken (the operation is read-only with respect to the destination).
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--restore DIR] <source-dir> <destination-dir>" >&2
}

help() {
  local prog
  prog=$(basename "$0")
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $prog [--keep-daily N] [--keep-weekly N] [--verify] [--exclude PATTERN]... [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--restore DIR] <source-dir> <destination-dir>

Create a tar.gz backup of <source-dir> inside <destination-dir>, named
<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (timestamp in UTC), then rotate out
older archives. Retention keeps the union of the --keep-daily newest archives
and the newest archive from each of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks.

Options:
  --keep-daily N   Number of newest archives to keep (default: 7)
  --keep-weekly N  Additionally keep the newest archive from each of the last
                   N ISO weeks (Mon-Sun), counted back from the current UTC
                   week inclusive; 0 disables it (default: 4)
  --verify         After writing, list the archive contents with
                   tar -tzf and fail if the listing is empty
  --exclude PAT    Exclude files matching PAT from the archive (passed
                   to tar as --exclude); may be given multiple times
  --restore DIR    Restore-only mode: extract the newest archive from
                   <destination-dir> into DIR (creating DIR if needed).
                   Refuses a DIR that exists and is not empty. No new backup
                   is created and no lock is taken.
  --dry-run        Print what would be created and deleted (plain "would
                   create: <path>" / "would delete: <path>" lines) without
                   touching anything
  --quiet          Suppress all informational output (created/removed/verify
                   lines and dry-run lines); errors still go to stderr
  -h, --help       Show this help and exit
EOF
}

# Print an informational message to stdout, unless --quiet is set. Errors are
# always printed separately to stderr; this only governs status output.
log() {
  if (( ! quiet )); then
    echo "$@"
  fi
}

# Monotonic integer index of the ISO week (Mon-Sun) that contains YYYYMMDD:
# (epoch of that week's Monday, UTC) / 604800. Consecutive ISO weeks differ by
# exactly 1 regardless of the year, leap weeks (53), or the Jan-1/Dec-31
# boundary — unlike %V/%G, which wrap around year edges.
iso_week_index() {
  local d="$1"
  local dash="${d:0:4}-${d:4:2}-${d:6:2}"
  local out epoch dow mon
  out=$(date -u -d "$dash" '+%s %u')
  epoch=${out%% *}
  dow=${out##* }
  mon=$(( epoch - (dow - 1) * 86400 ))
  echo $(( mon / 604800 ))
}

# Print the basenames in $1 that match <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz, one per
# line. Fixed-width UTC timestamps make lexicographic order equal to
# chronological order, so a caller can `| sort -r` for newest-first. This is the
# single place that defines "our" archives; both rotation (deletion candidates)
# and --restore (newest pick) use it, so they always agree on the pattern.
list_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2"
  local f b
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$b"
    fi

}

# basenames from the $1/*.tar.gz glob matching <base>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz,

# newest archive of each of the last $5 ISO weeks (0 disables it).
# $4 (optional) is the number of not-yet-existing archives a real run would
# add before rotation (1 for --dry-run); it shifts the daily keep threshold so
# the dry report matches a real run. Weekly retention is anchored to the
# current UTC week, which an incoming archive cannot move, so it is not shifted.
rotate_old_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" keep="$3" incoming="${4:-0}" keep_weekly="${5:-0}"
  local -a candidates=()
  local b i total sorted

  sorted=$(list_archives "$dest" "$base" | sort -r)
  if [[ -n "$sorted" ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r b; do
      candidates+=("$b")
    done <<< "$sorted"
  fi

  total=$(( ${#candidates[@]} + incoming ))
  if (( total <= keep )); then
    return 0
  fi

  # Build the keep set (basenames) from both retention rules.
  local -A keep_set=()
  i=0
  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if (( i + incoming < keep )); then
      keep_set["$b"]=1
    fi
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
  done <<< "$sorted"

  if (( keep_weekly > 0 )); then
    local now_week min_week
    now_week=$(iso_week_index "$(date -u +%Y%m%d)")
    min_week=$(( now_week - keep_weekly + 1 ))
    local -A seen_week=()
    local stem date8 wk
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r b; do
      stem="${b#"$base"-}"
      date8="${stem:0:8}"
      wk=$(iso_week_index "$date8")
      # Scanning newest-first, the first archive seen for a week is its newest.
      if (( wk >= min_week && wk <= now_week )) && [[ -z "${seen_week[$wk]:-}" ]]; then
        keep_set["$b"]=1
        seen_week["$wk"]=1
      fi
      i=$(( i + 1 ))
    done <<< "$sorted"
  fi

  while IFS= read -r b; do
    if [[ -z "${keep_set[$b]:-}" ]]; then
      if (( dry_run )); then
        log "would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"
      else
        log "Removing old archive: ${dest%/}/$b"
        rm -- "${dest%/}/$b"
      fi
    fi
  done <<< "$sorted"
}

# Extract the newest matching archive from $2 into $3, creating $3 if it does
# not exist. Read-only with respect to $2 (it only reads the archive it picks),
# so it takes no destination lock: a concurrent backup is at worst a harmless
# race that surfaces as a clear tar error. Refuses (exit 2) if $3 exists and is
# not a directory, or if it is a non-empty directory. With --dry-run it reports
# the action via log (so --quiet can suppress it) and touches nothing.
do_restore() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2" target="$3"
  local newest

  newest=$(list_archives "$dest" "$base" | sort -r)
  if [[ -n "$newest" ]]; then
    newest="${newest%%$'\n'*}"
  fi
  if [[ -z "$newest" ]]; then
    echo "Error: no ${base}-*.tar.gz archive found in '$dest' to restore" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ -e "$target" && ! -d "$target" ]]; then
    echo "Error: restore target '$target' exists and is not a directory" >&2
    return 2
  fi
  if [[ -d "$target" ]] && [[ -n "$(find "$target" -mindepth 1 -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    echo "Error: restore target '$target' is not empty; clear it first" >&2
    return 2
  fi

  if (( dry_run )); then
    log "would extract: ${dest%/}/${newest} into ${target%/}"
    return 0
  fi

  mkdir -p -- "$target"
  if ! tar -xzf "${dest%/}/${newest}" -C "$target"; then
    echo "Error: failed to extract '${dest%/}/${newest}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  log "Restored ${dest%/}/${newest} into ${target%/}"
  return 0
}

keep_daily=7
keep_weekly=4
verify=0
excludes=()
dry_run=0
quiet=0
restore_dir=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep-daily)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-daily requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_daily="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-daily=*)
      keep_daily="${1#--keep-daily=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --keep-weekly)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
        echo "Error: --keep-weekly requires a value" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      keep_weekly="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --keep-weekly=*)
      keep_weekly="${1#--keep-weekly=}"
      shift
      ;;
    --verify)
      verify=1
      shift
      ;;
    --exclude)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("$2")
      shift 2
      ;;
    --exclude=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--exclude=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --exclude requires a non-empty pattern" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      excludes+=("${1#--exclude=}")
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run)
      dry_run=1
      shift
      ;;
    --quiet)
      quiet=1
      shift
      ;;
    --restore)
      if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --restore requires a target directory" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      restore_dir="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --restore=*)
      if [[ -z "${1#--restore=}" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --restore requires a target directory" >&2
        usage
        exit 2
      fi
      restore_dir="${1#--restore=}"
      shift
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      help
      exit 0
      ;;
    -*)
      echo "Error: unknown option '$1'" >&2
      usage
      exit 2
      ;;
    *)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ $# -ne 2 ]]; then
  usage
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_daily" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-daily must be a positive integer (got '$keep_daily')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! "$keep_weekly" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: --keep-weekly must be a non-negative integer (got '$keep_weekly')" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source="${1%/}"
dest="$2"

if [[ -z "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory must not be empty" >&2
  exit 2
fi

base=$(basename "$source")

# Restore-only mode: read-only on $dest; runs before the lock and before any
# mutation. A non-zero return (1: no archive; 2: bad target) trips set -e with
# the right code; on success we exit 0 without touching the backup path.
if [[ -n "$restore_dir" ]]; then
  do_restore "$dest" "$base" "$restore_dir"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ ! -d "$source" ]]; then
  echo "Error: source directory '$source' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if (( ! dry_run )); then
  mkdir -p "$dest"

  # Hold an exclusive lock for the rest of the run so two runs cannot
  # rotate at the same time. Prefer flock(1) when available; otherwise
  # fall back to a noclobber pidfile (a stale lock is detected via the
  # recorded pid and taken over). The lock file lives in the
  # destination and is not a *.tar.gz, so rotation never touches it.
  lockfile="$dest/backup-${base}.lock"
  lock_acquired=0
  lock_use_flock=0
  cleanup_lock() {
    if (( lock_acquired )) && (( ! lock_use_flock )); then
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
    fi
  }
  trap cleanup_lock EXIT
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    lock_use_flock=1
    exec 9>"$lockfile"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
      echo "Error: another backup run holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
  else
    if ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
      lock_acquired=1
    else
      holder=$(cat "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [[ "$holder" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: another backup run (pid $holder) holds the lock '$lockfile'; try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      echo "Warning: removing stale lock file '$lockfile'" >&2
      rm -f -- "$lockfile"
      if ! ( set -o noclobber; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: could not acquire the lock '$lockfile' (contended); try again later" >&2
        exit 3
      fi
      lock_acquired=1
    fi
  fi
fi

stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
archive="$dest/${base}-${stamp}.tar.gz"

if (( dry_run )); then
  # Report what would happen without touching anything (no mkdir, no
  # tar, no rm); incoming=1 accounts for the archive a real run would
  # create first, so the delete report matches a real run.
  log "would create: $archive"
  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 1 "$keep_weekly"
else
  # Archive the source directory by name from its parent, so paths
  # inside the archive are relative (e.g. <base>/file.txt).
  tar_args=(-czf "$archive" -C "$(dirname "$source")")
  if (( ${#excludes[@]} > 0 )); then
    for pattern in "${excludes[@]}"; do
      tar_args+=(--exclude "$pattern")
    done
  fi
  tar_args+=("$base")
  tar "${tar_args[@]}"

  log "Created $archive"

  if (( verify )); then
    listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
    if [[ -z "$listing" ]]; then
      echo "Error: verification failed: '$archive' lists no entries" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    log "Verified $archive (listing is non-empty)"
  fi

  rotate_old_archives "$dest" "$base" "$keep_daily" 0 "$keep_weekly"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Tests for bin/backup.sh:
#   1. basic backup: archive created, name format, contents
#   2. rotation with the default keep-daily count (7); stray files
#      (inside dest not matching the pattern, outside dest matching it)
#      must survive
#   3. rotation honoring --keep-daily 3
#   4. --keep-daily validation
#   5. --help output
#   6. --verify: succeeds on a good archive, fails on an empty listing
#   7. --exclude (repeatable): a .cache dir in the source is left out
#   8. --dry-run: reports create/delete as plain lines, touches nothing
#   9. missing source directory: error to stderr, exit 2, nothing printed
#      to stdout
#   10. lock file: a concurrent second run exits 3; the first run still
#        completes and creates its archive
#   11. --keep-weekly retention across six weeks: the keep set is the union of
#        the daily keep set and the newest archive of each of the last N ISO
#        weeks (covers daily-only, weekly-only, and window-edge cases)
#   12. --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention
#   13. --keep-weekly validation (negative / non-numeric rejected, 0 ok)
#   14. --quiet: a successful run prints nothing to stdout (but still does
#        the work); errors still go to stderr
#   15. --restore: extracts the newest matching archive into a target dir;
#        a non-empty target is refused; no matching archive is an error
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

source_dir="$tmpdir/source"
dest_dir="$tmpdir/backups"

mkdir -p "$source_dir/data"
echo "hello" > "$source_dir/data/file1.txt"
echo "world" > "$source_dir/file2.txt"

fail() {
  echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Count archives in $1 that match <source basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.
count_archives() {
  local dest="$1" base="$2"
  local n=0 f b
  for f in "$dest"/*.tar.gz; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(basename "$f")
    if [[ "$b" =~ ^"$base"-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$ ]]; then
      n=$(( n + 1 ))
    fi
  done
  printf '%s' "$n"
}

# Create fake "old" archives in $1 named source-202601DD-000000.tar.gz
# for January days $2..$3 (fixed past dates, one file per day).
make_fake_archives() {
  local dest="$1" first="$2" last="$3"
  local i f
  for (( i = first; i <= last; i++ )); do
    f="$dest/source-202601$(printf '%02d' "$i")-000000.tar.gz"
    touch "$f"
  done
}

# Compute YYYYMMDD for a date relative to the current ISO week: $1 = number of
# weeks before this week (0 = this week), $2 = day offset into that week
# (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday). Anchoring to the real current week keeps the
# weekly fixtures correct no matter which day of the week the suite runs on.
week_date() {
  local weeks_back="$1" day_offset="$2"
  local dow monday_epoch target
  dow=$(date -u +%u)
  monday_epoch=$(date -u -d "today - $((dow - 1)) days" +%s)
  target=$(( monday_epoch - weeks_back * 7 * 86400 + day_offset * 86400 ))
  date -u -d "@$target" +%Y%m%d
}

echo "--- Test 1: basic backup ---"
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_dir"

shopt -s nullglob
archives=("$dest_dir"/*.tar.gz)
[[ ${#archives[@]} -gt 0 ]] || fail "no archive found in $dest_dir"
archive="${archives[0]}"
echo "Archive: $archive"

name=$(basename "$archive")
re="^$(basename "$source_dir")-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}\.tar\.gz$"
[[ "$name" =~ $re ]] || fail "archive name '$name' does not match <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz"

listing=$(tar -tzf "$archive")
[[ "$listing" == *"source/data/file1.txt"* ]] || fail "archive is missing source/data/file1.txt"
[[ "$listing" == *"source/file2.txt"* ]] || fail "archive is missing source/file2.txt"
echo "PASS: basic backup"

echo "--- Test 2: rotation with default keep (7) ---"
dest_rot="$tmpdir/backups-rotation"
mkdir -p "$dest_rot"
make_fake_archives "$dest_rot" 1 10

# Stray files that must survive rotation:
#  - inside dest, not matching the archive name pattern
#  - inside dest, a .tar.gz but not matching the timestamp pattern
#  - outside dest, matching the archive name pattern
stray_notes="$dest_rot/notes.txt"
stray_tarball="$dest_rot/source-not-an-archive.tar.gz"
stray_outside="$tmpdir/source-20260115-000000.tar.gz"
echo "keep me" > "$stray_notes"
touch "$stray_tarball"
touch "$stray_outside"

# --keep-weekly 0 isolates the daily rule so this test is correct regardless
# of when it runs (the January fixtures would otherwise be inside the weekly
# window if the suite happened to run in early 2026).
bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_rot"

count=$(count_archives "$dest_rot" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 7 ]] || fail "expected 7 archives after rotation, found $count"

i=1
while (( i <= 10 )); do
  f="$dest_rot/source-202601$(printf '%02d' "$i")-000000.tar.gz"
  if (( i <= 4 )); then
    [[ ! -e "$f" ]] || fail "old archive $f should have been deleted"
  else
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || fail "archive $f should have been kept"
  fi
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done

[[ -e "$stray_notes" ]] || fail "stray file $stray_notes was deleted by rotation"
[[ -e "$stray_tarball" ]] || fail "non-matching file $stray_tarball was deleted by rotation"
[[ -e "$stray_outside" ]] || fail "file outside destination $stray_outside was deleted by rotation"
echo "PASS: rotation keeps the 7 newest (default)"

echo "--- Test 3: rotation with --keep-daily 3 ---"
dest_opt="$tmpdir/backups-keep3"
mkdir -p "$dest_opt"
make_fake_archives "$dest_opt" 1 10

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 3 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_opt"

count=$(count_archives "$dest_opt" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 3 ]] || fail "expected 3 archives after rotation, found $count"
[[ -e "$dest_opt/source-20260109-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "source-20260109-000000.tar.gz should have been kept"
[[ -e "$dest_opt/source-20260110-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "source-20260110-000000.tar.gz should have been kept"
echo "PASS: --keep-daily 3 honored"

echo "--- Test 4: --keep-daily validation ---"
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-daily 0 should have been rejected"
fi
echo "PASS: --keep-daily 0 rejected"

echo "--- Test 5: --help ---"
if ! help_out=$(bash bin/backup.sh --help 2>&1); then
  fail "--help should exit successfully"
fi
[[ "$help_out" == *"Usage:"* ]] || fail "--help output is missing the usage line"
[[ "$help_out" == *"--keep-daily"* ]] || fail "--help output is missing the --keep-daily option"
echo "PASS: --help"

echo "--- Test 6: --verify ---"
dest_verify="$tmpdir/backups-verify"
verify_out="$tmpdir/verify-out.txt"
bash bin/backup.sh --verify "$source_dir" "$dest_verify" > "$verify_out" 2>&1 || fail "--verify run should have succeeded"
grep -q "Verified" "$verify_out" || fail "--verify run did not report verification"

# Force an empty listing: stub tar -tzf to print nothing
real_tar=$(command -v tar)
fakebin="$tmpdir/fakebin"
mkdir -p "$fakebin"
cat > "$fakebin/tar" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [[ \"\$1\" == \"-tzf\" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi
exec \"$real_tar\" \"\$@\"
EOF
chmod +x "$fakebin/tar"

if PATH="$fakebin:$PATH" bash bin/backup.sh --verify "$source_dir" "$dest_verify" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--verify should fail when the listing is empty"
fi
echo "PASS: --verify"

echo "--- Test 7: --exclude (repeatable) ---"
source_excl="$tmpdir/source-excl"
mkdir -p "$source_excl/.cache"
echo "important" > "$source_excl/data.txt"
echo "note" > "$source_excl/notes.tmp"
echo "junk" > "$source_excl/.cache/tmp.bin"

# Control run: without --exclude, .cache must be in the archive
dest_excl_all="$tmpdir/backups-excl-all"
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_excl" "$dest_excl_all" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "control run without --exclude failed"
mapfile -t archives_all < <(find "$dest_excl_all" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' | sort -r)
listing_all=$(tar -tzf "${archives_all[0]}")
[[ "$listing_all" == *".cache"* ]] || fail "control: .cache should be present without --exclude"

# With two --exclude options, both must be absent
dest_excl="$tmpdir/backups-excl"
bash bin/backup.sh --exclude .cache --exclude notes.tmp "$source_excl" "$dest_excl" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "--exclude run failed"
mapfile -t archives_excl < <(find "$dest_excl" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' | sort -r)
[[ ${#archives_excl[@]} -eq 1 ]] || fail "expected 1 archive after --exclude run, found ${#archives_excl[@]}"
listing=$(tar -tzf "${archives_excl[0]}")
if [[ "$listing" == *".cache"* ]]; then
  fail ".cache was not excluded from the archive"
fi
if [[ "$listing" == *"notes.tmp"* ]]; then
  fail "notes.tmp was not excluded from the archive"
fi
[[ "$listing" == *"source-excl/data.txt"* ]] || fail "data.txt missing from excluded-run archive"
echo "PASS: --exclude (repeatable)"

echo "--- Test 8: --dry-run ---"
dest_dry="$tmpdir/backups-dry"
mkdir -p "$dest_dry"
make_fake_archives "$dest_dry" 1 10

dry_out="$tmpdir/dry-out.txt"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_dry" > "$dry_out" 2>&1 || fail "--dry-run should succeed"

grep -q "^would create: $dest_dry/source-[0-9]\{8\}-[0-9]\{6\}\.tar\.gz$" "$dry_out" \
  || fail "missing create line for the new archive"

del_count=$(grep -c "^would delete: " "$dry_out" || true)
# 10 existing + 1 to-be-created = 11, keep 7 => 4 oldest would be deleted
[[ "$del_count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 delete lines, got $del_count"

# nothing was touched: all 10 fakes remain, no new archive was created
count=$(count_archives "$dest_dry" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 10 ]] || fail "dry-run changed the archive count: $count"

# a missing destination directory is not created either
dest_dry_new="$tmpdir/backups-dry-new"
bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dry_new" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "--dry-run with missing dest should succeed"
[[ ! -e "$dest_dry_new" ]] || fail "dry-run created the destination directory"
echo "PASS: --dry-run"

echo "--- Test 9: missing source directory ---"
missing_src="$tmpdir/does-not-exist"
missing_out="$tmpdir/missing-out.txt"
missing_err="$tmpdir/missing-err.txt"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$missing_src" "$dest_dir" > "$missing_out" 2> "$missing_err"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected exit 2 for missing source, got $rc"
grep -q "source directory" "$missing_err" || fail "stderr does not mention the missing source directory"
[[ ! -s "$missing_out" ]] || fail "expected no stdout output for missing source"
echo "PASS: missing source exits 2"

# 10. Locking: while another process holds the destination lock, a second run
#     exits 3 with a clear message and creates nothing; once the holder
#     releases, a normal run succeeds. The test holds the same lock file the
#     script uses, so the contention is deterministic (no timing dependence).
echo "--- Test 10: lock file prevents concurrent runs ---"
dest_lock="$tmpdir/backups-lock"
mkdir -p "$dest_lock"
make_fake_archives "$dest_lock" 1 3

lockfile="$dest_lock/backup-source.lock"

if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # Hold the lock for 5 seconds; flock releases it when the command exits.
  flock "$lockfile" -c 'sleep 5' &
  holder=$!
  # Wait until the holder actually holds it. The probe only briefly grabs the
  # lock while it is free, and nothing else contends during this window.
  for (( attempt = 0; attempt < 100; attempt++ )); do
    if ! flock -n "$lockfile" -c true 2>/dev/null; then
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.1
  done
else
  # No flock: emulate the fallback protocol with a pidfile holding a live pid;
  # the script must treat it as a held lock.
  sleep 5 &
  holder=$!
  printf '%s\n' "$holder" > "$lockfile"
  sleep 0.2
fi

lock_out2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.out"
lock_err2="$tmpdir/lock-run2.err"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out2" 2> "$lock_err2"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]] || fail "second concurrent run should exit 3, got $rc"
grep -qi "lock" "$lock_err2" || fail "stderr of the locked-out run does not mention the lock: $(cat "$lock_err2")"
[[ -z "$(cat "$lock_out2")" ]] || fail "locked-out run printed to stdout"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 3 ]] || fail "locked-out run changed the archive count: $count"

# Once the holder releases, a normal run succeeds and creates its archive.
wait "$holder" || fail "lock holder should have exited"
lock_out3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.out"
lock_err3="$tmpdir/lock-run3.err"
set +e
bash bin/backup.sh "$source_dir" "$dest_lock" > "$lock_out3" 2> "$lock_err3"
rc=$?
set -e
[[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || fail "run after lock release should succeed, got $rc (stderr: $(cat "$lock_err3"))"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_lock" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 4 ]] || fail "expected 4 archives after released run (3 fakes + new), got $count"
echo "PASS: lock file prevents concurrent runs (exit 3)"

# 11. Weekly retention across six ISO weeks. The keep set is the union of
#     (a) the --keep-daily newest archives and (b) the newest archive of each
#     of the last --keep-weekly ISO weeks (window [now-N+1, now]). The fixtures
#     are spread over six weeks, with several archives in some weeks, so the
#     test reaches every branch of the policy: a daily-only survivor, weekly-only
#     survivors in three different in-window weeks, the oldest week still inside
#     the window (inclusive edge), a week just outside the window, and non-newest
#     archives inside in-window weeks.
#     keep_daily=2 keeps {new archive, w0a}; keep_weekly=4 covers weeks
#     W0..W-3, so the newest of W-1 / W-2 / W-3 also survives.
echo "--- Test 11: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks ---"
dest_wk="$tmpdir/backups-weekly"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk"
# Fakes are stamped at 00:00:00 so the real archive (created now) is always the
# newest in the current week. Only day 0 is used in the current week so it can
# never be in the future, regardless of what day of the week the suite runs on.
w0a=$(week_date 0 0)   # W0  Mon  -> kept by DAILY only (the real archive is W0's newest)
w1a=$(week_date 1 0)   # W-1 Mon  -> deleted (not the newest of W-1)
w1b=$(week_date 1 4)   # W-1 Fri  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-1)
w2a=$(week_date 2 1)   # W-2 Tue  -> deleted (not the newest of W-2)
w2b=$(week_date 2 5)   # W-2 Sat  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-2)
w3=$(week_date 3 2)    # W-3 Wed  -> kept by WEEKLY (newest of W-3, oldest week in window)
w4=$(week_date 4 3)    # W-4 Thu  -> deleted (just outside the window)
w5a=$(week_date 5 1)   # W-5 Tue  -> deleted (outside the window)
w5b=$(week_date 5 5)   # W-5 Sat  -> deleted (outside the window)
for n in "$w0a" "$w1a" "$w1b" "$w2a" "$w2b" "$w3" "$w4" "$w5a" "$w5b"; do
  touch "$dest_wk/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 4 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk"

# Daily-only survivor: the real archive is the newest of W0, so the weekly rule
# keeps the real one (not w0a); w0a survives solely via the daily rule.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a (daily-only survivor) should be kept"
# Weekly-only survivors: the newest archive of each in-window week.
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b (newest of W-1) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b (newest of W-2) should be kept by the weekly rule"
[[ -e "$dest_wk/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 (newest of W-3, window edge) should be kept by the weekly rule"
# Non-newest archives inside in-window weeks are deleted.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w1a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1a (not newest of W-1) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w2a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2a (not newest of W-2) should be deleted"
# Weeks outside the weekly window are deleted (none of them are in the daily set).
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w4}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w4 (W-4, just outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5a (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk/source-${w5b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w5b (W-5, outside the window) should be deleted"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk" source)
# Kept: new archive + w0a + w1b + w2b + w3 = 5; deleted: w1a w2a w4 w5a w5b.
[[ "$count" -eq 5 ]] || fail "expected 5 archives after six-week rotation, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly retention across six weeks"

# 12. --keep-weekly 0: with the same six-week fixtures, the weekly rule is off,
#     so only the daily set survives. The archives that test 11 kept purely by
#     the weekly rule (w1b, w2b, w3) must now be deleted.
echo "--- Test 12: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention ---"
dest_wk0="$tmpdir/backups-weekly0"
mkdir -p "$dest_wk0"
for n in "$w0a" "$w1a" "$w1b" "$w2a" "$w2b" "$w3" "$w4" "$w5a" "$w5b"; do
  touch "$dest_wk0/source-${n}-000000.tar.gz"
done

bash bin/backup.sh --keep-daily 2 --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_wk0"

# Only the 2 newest survive: the new archive + w0a.
[[ -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w0a}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w0a should be kept by the daily rule"
# The weekly-only survivors from test 11 are now gone, proving the weekly
# rule is disabled.
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w1b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w1b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w2b}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w2b should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
[[ ! -e "$dest_wk0/source-${w3}-000000.tar.gz" ]] || fail "w3 should be deleted when weekly is disabled"
count=$(count_archives "$dest_wk0" source)
[[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || fail "expected 2 archives with weekly disabled, found $count"
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly 0 disables weekly retention"

# 13. --keep-weekly validation: 0 and positive integers are accepted; negative
#     and non-numeric values are rejected with exit 2.
echo "--- Test 13: --keep-weekly validation ---"
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly -1 "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly -1 should have been rejected"
fi
if bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly abc "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly abc should have been rejected"
fi
if ! bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--keep-weekly 0 should be accepted"
fi
echo "PASS: --keep-weekly validation"

# 14. --quiet: on a successful run nothing is printed to stdout, but the
#     backup still happens. Errors still reach stderr. Dry-run lines are
#     also suppressed under --quiet.
echo "--- Test 14: --quiet prints errors and nothing else ---"
dest_q="$tmpdir/backups-quiet"
q_out="$(bash bin/backup.sh --quiet "$source_dir" "$dest_q")"
[[ -z "$q_out" ]] || fail "--quiet run should print nothing to stdout (got: $q_out)"
n=$(count_archives "$dest_q" source)
[[ "$n" -eq 1 ]] || fail "quiet run should still create the archive (found $n)"

q_dry_out="$(bash bin/backup.sh --quiet --dry-run "$source_dir" "$dest_q")"
[[ -z "$q_dry_out" ]] || fail "--quiet --dry-run should print nothing to stdout (got: $q_dry_out)"

# An argument error is still reported on stderr, and stdout stays empty.
q_err_out="$(bash bin/backup.sh --quiet "$tmpdir/no-such-src" "$dest_q" 2>"$tmpdir/q.err")" || true
q_err_err="$(cat "$tmpdir/q.err")"
[[ -z "$q_err_out" ]] || fail "quiet error run should print nothing to stdout (got: $q_err_out)"
[[ "$q_err_err" == *"Error"* ]] || fail "quiet error run should still print the error to stderr (got: $q_err_err)"
echo "PASS: --quiet prints errors and nothing else"

# 15. --restore: extract the newest matching archive into a target directory.
#     The archive's top-level entry is the source basename, so files land in
#     <target>/<source-basename>/.... A non-empty target is refused (exit 2);
#     a destination with no matching archive is an error (exit 1). The source
#     directory itself need not exist (only its basename drives matching).
echo "--- Test 15: --restore extracts the newest archive ---"
dest_rst="$tmpdir/backups-restore"
bash bin/backup.sh --keep-weekly 0 "$source_dir" "$dest_rst" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "restore setup: backup run failed"
n=$(count_archives "$dest_rst" source)
[[ "$n" -eq 1 ]] || fail "restore setup: expected 1 archive in $dest_rst, found $n"

# (a) Restore into a brand-new target: succeeds, target created, content correct.
tgt_new="$tmpdir/restore-new"
r_out="$(bash bin/backup.sh --restore "$tgt_new" "$source_dir" "$dest_rst")" || fail "restore into a fresh target should succeed"
[[ "$r_out" == *"Restored "* ]] || fail "restore should print a Restored line (got: $r_out)"
[[ -d "$tgt_new" ]] || fail "restore should have created the target dir"
[[ -f "$tgt_new/source/data/file1.txt" ]] || fail "restore should extract source/data/file1.txt"
[[ "$(cat "$tgt_new/source/data/file1.txt")" == "hello" ]] || fail "restored data/file1.txt content mismatch"
[[ "$(cat "$tgt_new/source/file2.txt")" == "world" ]] || fail "restored file2.txt content mismatch"

# (b) Restore into an existing empty directory: also succeeds.
tgt_empty="$tmpdir/restore-empty"
mkdir -p "$tgt_empty"
bash bin/backup.sh --restore "$tgt_empty" "$source_dir" "$dest_rst" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "restore into an existing empty dir should succeed"
[[ -f "$tgt_empty/source/file2.txt" ]] || fail "restore into an empty dir should extract source/file2.txt"

# (c) Restore into a non-empty target: refused (exit 2), target unchanged.
tgt_full="$tmpdir/restore-full"
mkdir -p "$tgt_full"
echo "x" > "$tgt_full/occupied.txt"
if bash bin/backup.sh --restore "$tgt_full" "$source_dir" "$dest_rst" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "restore into a non-empty target should be refused"
fi

# (d) A destination with no matching archive: error (exit 1).
dest_empty="$tmpdir/backups-restore-empty"
mkdir -p "$dest_empty"
if bash bin/backup.sh --restore "$tmpdir/restore-none" "$source_dir" "$dest_empty" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "restore with no matching archive should fail"
fi

# (e) --restore= with an empty value: rejected (exit 2).
if bash bin/backup.sh --restore= "$source_dir" "$dest_rst" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fail "--restore= with an empty value should be rejected"
fi

# (f) --dry-run --restore: prints a would-extract line, creates no target.
tgt_dry="$tmpdir/restore-dry"
dr_out="$(bash bin/backup.sh --dry-run --restore "$tgt_dry" "$source_dir" "$dest_rst")"
[[ "$dr_out" == *"would extract: "* ]] || fail "dry-run restore should print a would-extract line (got: $dr_out)"
[[ -d "$tgt_dry" ]] && fail "dry-run restore should not create the target"

# (g) The source directory need not exist for a restore: only its basename
#     drives archive matching, and the source-existence check is skipped in
#     restore mode. Use a missing path whose basename is still "source" so the
#     archive pattern matches.
tgt_ns="$tmpdir/restore-nosrc"
bash bin/backup.sh --restore "$tgt_ns" "$tmpdir/nonexistent/source" "$dest_rst" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "restore should not require the source directory to exist"
[[ -f "$tgt_ns/source/data/file1.txt" ]] || fail "restore with a missing source should still extract (basename drives matching)"

echo "PASS: --restore extracts the newest archive"

echo "PASS: all tests passed"

summary:
## Goal
Build a bash backup rotation tool in `/work/sh-backup/` that:
- Creates timestamped tar.gz backups of a source directory
- Rotates old archives (keeps N newest, deletes the rest)
- Supports `--keep-daily N` option (default 7), `--keep-weekly N` option (default 4), `--verify`, `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable), `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--restore DIR`, and `--help`
- `--keep-weekly N`: additionally keeps the newest archive from each of the last N ISO calendar weeks (Mon–Sun), in addition to `--keep-daily`
- `--quiet`: prints errors (stderr) and nothing else to stdout; informational output (Created/Removing/Verified/dry-run lines) suppressed
- `--restore DIR`: extracts the newest matching archive from the destination into DIR, refusing a non-empty target
- Exits with code 2 on argument errors (missing source, invalid `--keep-daily`, invalid `--keep-weekly`, unknown options)
- Uses a lock file in the destination to prevent concurrent rotation; second run exits 3 with a clear message
- Has a test suite covering all functionality
- Rotation must **never** delete anything outside the destination directory (structural guarantee, not incidental)
- Provides systemd timer + service example for daily scheduled runs
- Has a README.md documenting every option with an example of each

## Constraints & Preferences
- Every script must start with `set -euo pipefail`
- Quote every variable expansion (exception: `[[ =~ $re ]]` where `$re` must be unquoted for regex semantics)
- Archive naming: `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` with **UTC** time (`date -u`)
- Rotation only considers files matching the `<source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz` pattern (regex-anchored)
- Deletion is structurally scoped: candidates are collected as basenames from `"$dest"/*.tar.gz` and re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"` at deletion time
- Dry-run output uses plain `would create: <path>` / `would delete: <path>` lines (no mandatory prefix); the `DRY:` prefix rule has been lifted
- Exit code 2 for all argument/validation errors (missing source, `--keep-daily 0`, `--keep-weekly -1` or non-numeric, unknown options, non-empty restore target)
- Exit code 3 when another run holds the lock (clear message to stderr)
- Exit code 1 for runtime failures (no archive to restore, tar extraction failure)
- Use `flock` if available; fall back to a noclobber pidfile otherwise
- `flock(1)` in fd mode has a critical pitfall: `flock -n <fd>` in a shell with that fd open **acquires the lock on the shared OFD**, which persists as long as the shell's fd remains open. Must use `flock -n <file> -c true` form for non-destructive probing.
- `--keep-weekly` accepts non-negative integer (0 disables weekly retention); validated with `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`
- Weekly retention uses ISO weeks (Mon–Sun), anchored to current UTC week inclusive
- `iso_week_index` must be monotonic across year boundaries (use `monday_epoch / 604800`, not `%V`/`%G`)
- `--quiet` suppresses stdout only; stderr (errors, warnings) always shows
- `--help` is not affected by `--quiet` (explicit request still prints)
- **Argument order: options must come before positionals.** The parser `break`s on the first non-option arg; remaining `$@` must be exactly 2. Positionals-first invocation will fail with usage + exit 2.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` in `/work/sh-backup/`
- [x] `bin/backup.sh` — takes `<source-dir> <destination-dir>`, creates tar.gz, rotates old archives
- [x] `--keep-daily N` option (also `--keep-daily=N`), default 7, validated as positive integer
- [x] `--help` / `-h` option printing usage + option descriptions to stdout, exit 0
- [x] `rotate_old_archives()` function — regex-filters candidates as basenames, sorts newest-first, deletes beyond N, all deletions re-anchored to `"${dest%/}/<basename>"`
- [x] `--verify` flag — after writing, runs `tar -tzf "$archive"`; fails (exit 1) if listing is empty; verified **before** rotation
- [x] `--exclude PATTERN` (repeatable, also `--exclude=PATTERN`) — patterns passed to tar as `--exclude`; empty patterns rejected (exit 2); built into a `tar_args` array
- [x] `--dry-run` flag — prints `would create:` and `would delete:` lines; skips mkdir, tar, verify, rm
- [x] Missing source directory exits with code **2**, error to stderr
- [x] Lock file implementation in `bin/backup.sh` (flock + noclobber pidfile fallback, stale-lock detection, dry-run skips lock)
- [x] Test 10 rewritten with deterministic flock-based lock holding
- [x] E2E verification: two real runs contend correctly
- [x] Fallback (no-flock) path verified end-to-end
- [x] Commit `5030269` — "Add destination lock to prevent concurrent runs; missing source exits 2"
- [x] `iso_week_index` function: computes `monday_epoch / 604800`, gives monotonic values
- [x] Bash version confirmed: 5.3.9, `local -A` associative arrays work
- [x] All edits applied to `bin/backup.sh` for weekly retention
- [x] ShellCheck passes on `bin/backup.sh`
- [x] `week_date` helper added to `tests/run.sh`
- [x] Tests 2, 3, 8 modified to add `--keep-weekly 0` for date-robustness
- [x] **Test 11 redesigned to six-week spread**: keep_daily=2, keep_weekly=4, 9 fakes across W0–W-5. Expected: 5 kept, 5 deleted.
- [x] **Test 12 updated** to reuse the six-week fixtures with `--keep-weekly 0`. Expected: 2 kept.

| 5 | Deletion structurally scoped to dest | ✅ | candidates are basenames; every op re-anchored: `:178/180/181 …"${dest%/}/$b"` (incl. `rm --`) |
| 6 | Dry-run: plain `would create:` / `would delete:` | ✅ | `:421 log "would create: $archive"`, `:178 log "would delete: ${dest%/}/$b"` — no `DRY:` prefix |
